13048-
13049-I accept the referee corps’ paper-level verdict distribution: only quantization and MoE survive as new papers. I disagree with two cost conclusions inside those otherwise sound reviews:
13050-
13051:- The shrunk BF16/Q4/Q8 quantization paper costs **three**, not two, extension nights: one BF16 floor, one Q8 floor, and one contrast. Q4’s D-117 floor is the only free floor.
13052-- The re-anchored MoE paper costs **three to four**, not two, extension nights if the native MoE, forced-*k* MoE, and dense partner are all claim-bearing and therefore independently floored.
13053-
13054-Probabilities below are planning judgments, not statistical estimates. “4+N nights” means the corrected four-night MVP plus N extension nights.
13055-
13056-## Ranked portfolio
13057-
13058-### 1. `mvp-icpe-upgrade` — fund, but as the corrected metrology capstone
13059-
13060-The submitted “ICPE upgrade” was correctly judged WEAK because its cross-window Q4 prediction is unauthorized and its WT310E arm is neither necessary nor securely available. The surviving paper is nevertheless the highest-certainty and highest-priority portfolio item: the calibrated instrument, attribution limit, floor calculus, refusal protocol, D-117 floors, and prospective decode contrast. Add Window C’s held-out floor-validation ladder, not the proposed multi-night workload matrix. Honest cost is **four planned nights, about 11.2–13.2 quiet hours, 3–6 desk weeks, plus one reserved rerun slot**. Estimated first-pass survival of all four windows is only **60–70%** given the project’s history; completion with one governed reserve is roughly **80–90%**. This is the only item that must proceed regardless of every later ranking.
13061-
13062-### 2. `quantization-ladder` — the best second-paper bet
13063-
13064:The VIABLE verdict holds only after shrinking to **BF16/Q4/Q8**, deleting Q5/Q6, deleting the unbuilt JouleWise quality gate, and framing the result as precision- and kernel-specific *resolvability*, not quality-neutral efficiency. The D-117 1.5B Q4 floor and exact 128/512 workload carry directly into the paper. BF16 and Q8 still need their own floors, followed by a three-arm contrast: **4+3 nights**, **4–8 incremental desk weeks**, and one reserve slot. A BF16–Q4 result should be loud; Q4–Q8 is the scientifically useful anomaly test and may resolve or refuse. Estimated survival after the capability smoke is **65–75%**. This is lower novelty than a mechanism paper, but far lower operational risk and the best match to the priority rule.
13065-
13066-### 3. `moe-routing-energy` — stretch, re-anchored and more expensive
13067-
13068-The VIABLE judgment is persuasive, but the 65 GB Qwen3.5-122B VLM/hybrid reasoning checkpoint should not be the claim vehicle. Use the referee’s re-anchor: **Qwen3-30B-A3B versus a dense Qwen3-4B partner**, with native-*k* versus forced-*k* as the causal within-checkpoint leg. This gives the paper both an interpretable dense comparison and a mechanism intervention. It also creates three separately scoped floor cells—native MoE, forced-*k* MoE, and dense—so the honest cost is **4+3–4 nights**, **6–12 desk weeks**, and a reserve, not two nights. Routing-sidecar overhead, output-divergence-induced routing locality, and projected floors can all kill it before collection. Estimated pre-night survival is **35–50%**. This is the right stretch because its ceiling is much higher than quantization’s, not because it is safer.
13069-
13070-### 4. `floor-methodology-general` — absorb into the MVP; do not publish separately
13071-
13072-The referee was right: this has the portfolio’s best framing—“from repeatability to resolvability”—and an unfundable portability experiment. The NVML/RAPL battery neither transports the phase-attribution finding nor respects existing fences. The surviving content is the MVP’s intellectual packaging plus Window C’s held-out effect ladder. Cost is therefore **the same four MVP nights**, with roughly **1–3 additional desk weeks** for the ladder analysis, refusal taxonomy, and prose. Probability of a useful result is **70–80%** because both correct refusals and correct resolutions support the thesis. Rank four reflects its value to the capstone, not authorization for a second manuscript.
13073-
13074-### 5. `long-generation-dynamics` — retain the interior-chunk insight, redesign before any paper
13075-
13076-The proposal was WEAK because early-versus-late position is uncounterbalanceable and lacks a legitimate comparative floor. Its important discovery is different: attribution limitation is a **phase-boundary property**, not necessarily a global instrument property. Interior decode-chunk edges may be repeatability-limited near 0.3 J. First make that a desk-only MVP characterization figure. A later paper would need an intervention—bounded versus unbounded cache, or matched-position starting-KV variation—rather than observational token position. Claim-bearing cost is **4+1–2 nights** and **4–8 desk weeks** for chunk reduction, floor semantics, and refusal tests. Estimated survival after the runtime and floor gate is **45–60%**.
13077-
13078-### 6. `open-explore-registry` — keep only the prefix-reuse boundary/refusal paper
13079-
13080:The tag is WEAK as a three-paper portfolio, but its prefix-reuse idea is the only genuinely new asset-mined direction. The stated “crossover” is arithmetic—if building the cache is the avoided prefill, reuse wins at request two—while the empirical cache load/save overhead is probably below the instrument’s floor. The scientifically honest paper is therefore about what prefix reuse saves, what its SoC boundary misses in off-SoC cache I/O, and which overheads must be refused as unresolvable. Restrict to 2048/4096-token endpoints and mint matching gross/length floors inside **two extension windows**: **4+2 nights**, **3–5 desk weeks**, estimated survival **55–65%**. It is a credible alternate second paper if quantization dies at its desk gate.
13081-
13082-### 7. `kv-context-energy` — fund only a self-floored 1.5B endpoint study
13083-
13084:The original four-length, two-model “curve” is a borderline KILL: floor transport is anti-conservative, 7B faces the measured ~14 J comparative floor, and long-prefill thermal carryover is perfectly aligned with the claimed KV effect. A viable residue is one 1.5B long-context endpoint, longer decode to amplify the effect, a same-window long-context null floor, and a separate thermal-matched control. That is **two extension nights**, possibly three if the longer workload breaks the four-hour envelope: **4+2 planned, book 4+3**, with **3–6 desk weeks** and about **35–50%** survival. Do not arm 7B unless the fresh beta floor and local sizing independently support it.
13085-
13086-### 8. `spec-decode-energy` — buy only the two-hour option
13087-
13088-The paper remains WEAK: it needs a gross-request floor class, reopens a closed observability verdict, and existing local evidence shows speculative paths at only 0.36–0.41× baseline throughput. Its upside and alignment with Ed’s original goals still justify one cheap action: run the stock-runtime daytime tok/s pilot before a fork or floor work. Estimated probability that it survives that gate is only **15–25%**. If it unexpectedly passes, the honest program is **4+2–3 nights** and **6–12 desk weeks**; if spec-on is slower, close the paper immediately and report “does it ever repay?” as answered negatively at the feasibility level.
13089-

13177-## Synergy map
13178-
13179:- **Alpha’s Q4 floor is the central quantization saving.** Exact model, workload, runtime, phase and stack identity let Q4 serve as the middle quantization rung, eliminating one floor night.
13180-- **D-117’s pinset-v2 and multi-cell mint machinery lowers desk cost** for quantization and MoE, but it does not transport any numerical floor to a different stack.
13181-- **Window C can serve four MVP needs at once:** empirical floor behavior, magnitude/null response, linearity, and between-session evidence. It can inform later length-sweep transport rules, but does not automatically authorize them.
13182-- **The 203 idle captures are already collected as part of D-117.** The contamination analysis is therefore a zero-night evaluation of the admission gate.
13183-- **Refusal plumbing benefits every downstream paper.** Fixing it before Alpha gives the MVP, quantization, and MoE machine-attributable negative evidence.
13184-- **Quantization shares model, tokenizer, workload, adapter, manifest grammar and reporting with Alpha.** MoE shares only the generic machinery; its floors and attribution basis remain independent.
13185-- **The MoE dense and routed arms share runtime and tokenizer**, allowing one multi-arm science window, but each still needs a separate floor cell.
13186-- **A4 batch work and the spec-decode pilot are desk synergies, not reasons to fund batch nights.**
13187-- **GPU cadence benefits split feasibility only.** It cannot validate the Mac floor or a cross-device composite clock bound.

13189:## Single best second-paper bet: BF16/Q4/Q8 quantization
13190-
13191-Why it wins:
13192-
13193-- It has the most direct claim-grade reuse: Alpha supplies Q4’s floor.
13194-- It needs no new hardware, runtime fork, cross-device clock, serving policy, or unowned meter.
13195-- One contrast is almost guaranteed to resolve, while Q4–Q8 remains a real question.
13196-- A refusal is scientifically coherent: “these rungs cannot be ranked at this workload under the calibrated instrument.”
13197-- Its operational failures are mostly desk-visible before a night.
13198-

13251-## Ranked portfolio
13252-
13253-### 1. `mvp-icpe-upgrade` — fund, but as the corrected metrology capstone
13254-
13255-The submitted “ICPE upgrade” was correctly judged WEAK because its cross-window Q4 prediction is unauthorized and its WT310E arm is neither necessary nor securely available. The surviving paper is nevertheless the highest-certainty and highest-priority portfolio item: the calibrated instrument, attribution limit, floor calculus, refusal protocol, D-117 floors, and prospective decode contrast. Add Window C’s held-out floor-validation ladder, not the proposed multi-night workload matrix. Honest cost is **four planned nights, about 11.2–13.2 quiet hours, 3–6 desk weeks, plus one reserved rerun slot**. Estimated first-pass survival of all four windows is only **60–70%** given the project’s history; completion with one governed reserve is roughly **80–90%**. This is the only item that must proceed regardless of every later ranking.
13256-
13257-### 2. `quantization-ladder` — the best second-paper bet
13258-
13259:The VIABLE verdict holds only after shrinking to **BF16/Q4/Q8**, deleting Q5/Q6, deleting the unbuilt JouleWise quality gate, and framing the result as precision- and kernel-specific *resolvability*, not quality-neutral efficiency. The D-117 1.5B Q4 floor and exact 128/512 workload carry directly into the paper. BF16 and Q8 still need their own floors, followed by a three-arm contrast: **4+3 nights**, **4–8 incremental desk weeks**, and one reserve slot. A BF16–Q4 result should be loud; Q4–Q8 is the scientifically useful anomaly test and may resolve or refuse. Estimated survival after the capability smoke is **65–75%**. This is lower novelty than a mechanism paper, but far lower operational risk and the best match to the priority rule.
13260-
13261-### 3. `moe-routing-energy` — stretch, re-anchored and more expensive
13262-
13263-The VIABLE judgment is persuasive, but the 65 GB Qwen3.5-122B VLM/hybrid reasoning checkpoint should not be the claim vehicle. Use the referee’s re-anchor: **Qwen3-30B-A3B versus a dense Qwen3-4B partner**, with native-*k* versus forced-*k* as the causal within-checkpoint leg. This gives the paper both an interpretable dense comparison and a mechanism intervention. It also creates three separately scoped floor cells—native MoE, forced-*k* MoE, and dense—so the honest cost is **4+3–4 nights**, **6–12 desk weeks**, and a reserve, not two nights. Routing-sidecar overhead, output-divergence-induced routing locality, and projected floors can all kill it before collection. Estimated pre-night survival is **35–50%**. This is the right stretch because its ceiling is much higher than quantization’s, not because it is safer.
13264-
13265-### 4. `floor-methodology-general` — absorb into the MVP; do not publish separately
13266-
13267-The referee was right: this has the portfolio’s best framing—“from repeatability to resolvability”—and an unfundable portability experiment. The NVML/RAPL battery neither transports the phase-attribution finding nor respects existing fences. The surviving content is the MVP’s intellectual packaging plus Window C’s held-out effect ladder. Cost is therefore **the same four MVP nights**, with roughly **1–3 additional desk weeks** for the ladder analysis, refusal taxonomy, and prose. Probability of a useful result is **70–80%** because both correct refusals and correct resolutions support the thesis. Rank four reflects its value to the capstone, not authorization for a second manuscript.
13268-
13269-### 5. `long-generation-dynamics` — retain the interior-chunk insight, redesign before any paper
13270-
13271-The proposal was WEAK because early-versus-late position is uncounterbalanceable and lacks a legitimate comparative floor. Its important discovery is different: attribution limitation is a **phase-boundary property**, not necessarily a global instrument property. Interior decode-chunk edges may be repeatability-limited near 0.3 J. First make that a desk-only MVP characterization figure. A later paper would need an intervention—bounded versus unbounded cache, or matched-position starting-KV variation—rather than observational token position. Claim-bearing cost is **4+1–2 nights** and **4–8 desk weeks** for chunk reduction, floor semantics, and refusal tests. Estimated survival after the runtime and floor gate is **45–60%**.
13272-
13273-### 6. `open-explore-registry` — keep only the prefix-reuse boundary/refusal paper
13274-
13275:The tag is WEAK as a three-paper portfolio, but its prefix-reuse idea is the only genuinely new asset-mined direction. The stated “crossover” is arithmetic—if building the cache is the avoided prefill, reuse wins at request two—while the empirical cache load/save overhead is probably below the instrument’s floor. The scientifically honest paper is therefore about what prefix reuse saves, what its SoC boundary misses in off-SoC cache I/O, and which overheads must be refused as unresolvable. Restrict to 2048/4096-token endpoints and mint matching gross/length floors inside **two extension windows**: **4+2 nights**, **3–5 desk weeks**, estimated survival **55–65%**. It is a credible alternate second paper if quantization dies at its desk gate.
13276-
13277-### 7. `kv-context-energy` — fund only a self-floored 1.5B endpoint study
13278-
13279:The original four-length, two-model “curve” is a borderline KILL: floor transport is anti-conservative, 7B faces the measured ~14 J comparative floor, and long-prefill thermal carryover is perfectly aligned with the claimed KV effect. A viable residue is one 1.5B long-context endpoint, longer decode to amplify the effect, a same-window long-context null floor, and a separate thermal-matched control. That is **two extension nights**, possibly three if the longer workload breaks the four-hour envelope: **4+2 planned, book 4+3**, with **3–6 desk weeks** and about **35–50%** survival. Do not arm 7B unless the fresh beta floor and local sizing independently support it.
13280-
13281-### 8. `spec-decode-energy` — buy only the two-hour option
13282-
13283-The paper remains WEAK: it needs a gross-request floor class, reopens a closed observability verdict, and existing local evidence shows speculative paths at only 0.36–0.41× baseline throughput. Its upside and alignment with Ed’s original goals still justify one cheap action: run the stock-runtime daytime tok/s pilot before a fork or floor work. Estimated probability that it survives that gate is only **15–25%**. If it unexpectedly passes, the honest program is **4+2–3 nights** and **6–12 desk weeks**; if spec-on is slower, close the paper immediately and report “does it ever repay?” as answered negatively at the feasibility level.

== PROJECT BRIEF (state as of 2026-08-07) ==
JouleWise is Ed's undergraduate CS capstone: treating Apple's `powermetrics` software
power counter as a calibrated scientific instrument for phase-resolved (prefill vs
decode), single-request LLM inference energy on one named M3 Max stack (MLX, Qwen2.5
family, 4-bit). Core findings/machinery to date: in-window bracketed pulse-train
calibration of timing attribution; the instrument is ATTRIBUTION-LIMITED (~1 J per
phase member from ~30 ms edge uncertainty × ~33 W swings; repetition cannot average it
away), not noise-limited; detection floors composed from repeatability + worst-case
attribution + measured never-zero drift, published labelled; TWO separate claim gates
(floor clearance; interval-supported direction) with a practical ~5 J sizing bar for
phase contrasts; fail-closed collection protocol (pre-registration, admission gates,
ABBA counterbalancing, hash-bound custody chains, refusal log as evidence). MVP paper
draft is complete-in-structure (docs/paper/draft-v1.md) with demonstration values
pending. The claim path (decision D-117, adopted today): THREE fresh prospective quiet
windows — 1.5B decode floor, 7B decode floor, 1.5B-vs-7B decode contrast — each
live-bracketed under an issued calibration-acceptance regime; prefill floor cells ride
the floor windows; a 256-token prefill contrast arm is an open option (128-token
prefill contrast is MARGINAL vs the bar — custodied desk check).

mint pinsets, extraction specs, regression) → mint floors → populate the paper →
capstone submission; then an ICPE-class version.

492:This scope is deliberately narrow. A measurement characterizes one physical unit, operating-system build, runtime and library stack, model artifact, quantization, tokenizer, sampling policy, single-request execution policy, telemetry backend, and measurement boundary. It does not establish that an Apple hardware class or vendor is more efficient than another platform. Without an external power meter, absolute values remain internal to the named `powermetrics` system-on-chip boundary; same-boundary contrasts can still be scientifically useful when they pass the calibration and floor gates. Gross joules per request are the primary energy metric. Joules per prompt or output token are tokenizer-scoped companion metrics and are never treated as tokenizer-independent work units.
500:5. (C-v) demonstration measurements: phase-resolved J/token for two model sizes with a pre-registered contrast [+ quantization ladder if window budget allows];
523:JouleWise measures one sequential request at a time. Prompt processing (often called *prefill*) converts the input sequence into the model's internal state; token generation (often called *decode*) produces output tokens from that state. Because the experiment controls the runtime, it records the start and stop of these phases directly in the runtime event stream rather than inferring them from shapes in the power trace. The reducer then integrates the named `powermetrics` system-on-chip power channels between each pair of phase events using trapezoidal integration.
563:Point repeatability is not the full floor. Each energy value is an interval from the timing calibration in Section 3. The floor computation evaluates the complete point-floor estimator over the joint corners of all member intervals that pass the admission and evidence gates, then takes the largest value. For a null A/B/B/A block, the four signed member intervals are propagated through the contrast together. This corner calculation is deliberately conservative: a systematic boundary-placement error is not independent Gaussian noise, so adding it in root-sum-square form would understate the worst case. The published floor is no smaller than the largest accepted attribution width.
590:The floor is only one side of a claim decision. The calibrated floor bounds a false effect produced by the calibration condition; the confidence or decision interval for the particular measured contrast separately carries that contrast's timing-attribution uncertainty. These are distinct uses of the same physical uncertainty and both are required. The effective bar is therefore
596:where \(B_{\mathrm{claim}}\) is the claim-side measurement bound. For the measured phase-contrast regime, this combined bar is approximately 5 J. Neither term may be removed as an apparent double count. Effects below the floor are reported as *not resolvable*, not as zero, equal, or evidence of no difference. A directional claim is made only when the effect and its interval clear the applicable bar.
610:Comparisons use A/B/B/A blocks, abbreviated **ABBA**. Conditions A and B are measured in the order A, B, B, A, with ordinary cooldown between members. Averaging the two outer A observations and the two inner B observations cancels a linear time trend within the block to first order. For null-floor calibration, A and B are aliases of the exact same configuration and payload, so any nonzero block delta is a false comparative effect. For scientific contrasts, the A and B definitions are frozen in advance, and the contrast is computed within each block before blocks are aggregated. ABBA reduces common drift; it does not replace the measured whole-window drift allowance.
628:| Linearity | Hold the prompt profile fixed and ramp the requested output from 128 to 2048 tokens. Regress gross request and decode energy on the runtime-observed output count; inspect residual structure as well as the fitted slope. | Energy responds proportionally over the tested dynamic range, and the fitted per-token slope can serve as the known-effect standard for floor probes on this stack. It would not establish linearity outside the tested range or on another stack. | **[PENDING WINDOW C]** |
629:| Null response across magnitudes | Run identical A-equals-B ABBA blocks at short, medium, and long output magnitudes. Evaluate the paired deltas against zero and against the predicted decision envelopes. | The comparison path does not create a directional effect merely because total energy or duration changes, and false contrasts across the tested range are contained by the error model. A non-significant result alone is insufficient; the interval must be interpreted relative to the floor. | **[PENDING WINDOW C]** |
631:| Phase-attribution causal consistency | First compare the sum of separately integrated phase energies with the gross energy over their enclosing request. Then vary output length while holding prompt tokens fixed and fit the slope of prefill energy against output length. | Phase accounting is additive within its stated boundaries, and energy assigned to prefill does not acquire a systematic dependence on work that occurs later in decode. Together these tests challenge both missing energy and cross-phase leakage. | **[PENDING WINDOW C]** |
633:| Between-session stability | Repeat calibrations, null blocks, and floor cells across at least three sessions or days with the full stack identity recorded. | The calibration and floor are stable enough to reuse only under their declared freshness and identity rules, or reveal that a new session must mint a new floor. | **[PENDING WINDOW C]** |
637:The causal tests address the most important phase-specific risk. Additivity checks conservation inside the declared request boundary: phase intervals should reconcile with the enclosing total, subject to explicitly labeled setup or gap intervals. Causal invariance checks direction: holding the prompt fixed while increasing later decode work should not change energy attributed to earlier prefill. A nonzero prefill slope would indicate boundary leakage, shared-state coupling that invalidates the simple phase model, or both; it would narrow the claim rather than be explained away.
647:This section will report phase-resolved gross joules per request for two model sizes, with tokenizer-scoped joules per prompt token and per output token as companion metrics. It will contain the pre-registered same-boundary model-size contrast, its interval, the complete floor decomposition, the claim-side bound, the effect-to-floor ratio, and the final resolvable/unresolved verdict. No demonstration energy value from the superseded mint is carried into this draft. A quantization ladder will be included only if it is collected under its own stack-specific floors and the frozen window budget permits it.
655:The Illusion of Power Capping in LLM Decode samples graphics-processor power, integrates those samples, repeats configurations, and cross-checks sufficiently long operations against a separate hardware energy counter [IllusionPowerCapping]. This is a stronger measurement template than an unqualified software reading. Its counter agreement, run-to-run variation, snapshot fallback, and timing alignment nevertheless remain separate diagnostics rather than one bound on the reported effect, and its long sweeps do not use a drift-control ordering. JouleWise composes those classes of uncertainty into a decision rule for each contrast.
661:RAPL in Action established a validation agenda for commodity software counters: align lag before comparing streams, model wall power rather than assuming identity, account for temporal correlation, warm the system, measure sampler overhead, and inspect update granularity, overflow, jitter, and timestamp behavior [RAPLInAction]. Jay and Ostapenco likewise regress software readings against wall power and show that disagreement varies with load; they avoid claims about subtotals that the reference meter cannot observe [JayOstapenco]. JouleWise follows this epistemic boundary. A future external meter could test total gain and load dependence, but it would not validate how a total is divided between prefill and decode. The in-window pulse train addresses that distinct question.
669:This emphasis changes the role of failed runs. A rejected admission, stale calibration, contaminated member, or below-floor contrast is evidence about the instrument's operating domain. Hash-bound raw traces, runtime events, configurations, supersessions, verdicts, and pre-registration records make that evidence re-reducible. The refusal is retained rather than disappearing behind a final average.

2290:This scope is deliberately narrow. A measurement characterizes one physical unit, operating-system build, runtime and library stack, model artifact, quantization, tokenizer, sampling policy, single-request execution policy, telemetry backend, and measurement boundary. It does not establish that an Apple hardware class or vendor is more efficient than another platform. Without an external power meter, absolute values remain internal to the named `powermetrics` system-on-chip boundary; same-boundary contrasts can still be scientifically useful when they pass the calibration and floor gates. Gross joules per request are the primary energy metric. Joules per prompt or output token are tokenizer-scoped companion metrics and are never treated as tokenizer-independent work units.
2298:5. (C-v) demonstration measurements: phase-resolved J/token for two model sizes with a pre-registered contrast [+ quantization ladder if window budget allows];
2321:JouleWise measures one sequential request at a time. Prompt processing (often called *prefill*) converts the input sequence into the model's internal state; token generation (often called *decode*) produces output tokens from that state. Because the experiment controls the runtime, it records the start and stop of these phases directly in the runtime event stream rather than inferring them from shapes in the power trace. The reducer then integrates the named `powermetrics` system-on-chip power channels between each pair of phase events using trapezoidal integration.
2361:Point repeatability is not the full floor. Each energy value is an interval from the timing calibration in Section 3. The floor computation evaluates the complete point-floor estimator over the joint corners of all member intervals that pass the admission and evidence gates, then takes the largest value. For a null A/B/B/A block, the four signed member intervals are propagated through the contrast together. This corner calculation is deliberately conservative: a systematic boundary-placement error is not independent Gaussian noise, so adding it in root-sum-square form would understate the worst case. The published floor is no smaller than the largest accepted attribution width.
2388:The floor is only one side of a claim decision. The calibrated floor bounds a false effect produced by the calibration condition; the confidence or decision interval for the particular measured contrast separately carries that contrast's timing-attribution uncertainty. These are distinct uses of the same physical uncertainty and both are required. The effective bar is therefore
2394:where \(B_{\mathrm{claim}}\) is the claim-side measurement bound. For the measured phase-contrast regime, this combined bar is approximately 5 J. Neither term may be removed as an apparent double count. Effects below the floor are reported as *not resolvable*, not as zero, equal, or evidence of no difference. A directional claim is made only when the effect and its interval clear the applicable bar.
2408:Comparisons use A/B/B/A blocks, abbreviated **ABBA**. Conditions A and B are measured in the order A, B, B, A, with ordinary cooldown between members. Averaging the two outer A observations and the two inner B observations cancels a linear time trend within the block to first order. For null-floor calibration, A and B are aliases of the exact same configuration and payload, so any nonzero block delta is a false comparative effect. For scientific contrasts, the A and B definitions are frozen in advance, and the contrast is computed within each block before blocks are aggregated. ABBA reduces common drift; it does not replace the measured whole-window drift allowance.

Together these tests challenge both missing energy and cross-phase leakage. | **[PENDING WINDOW C]** |

2435:The causal tests address the most important phase-specific risk. Additivity checks conservation inside the declared request boundary: phase intervals should reconcile with the enclosing total, subject to explicitly labeled setup or gap intervals. Causal invariance checks direction: holding the prompt fixed while increasing later decode work should not change energy attributed to earlier prefill. A nonzero prefill slope would indicate boundary leakage, shared-state coupling that invalidates the simple phase model, or both; it would narrow the claim rather than be explained away.
2445:This section will report phase-resolved gross joules per request for two model sizes, with tokenizer-scoped joules per prompt token and per output token as companion metrics. It will contain the pre-registered same-boundary model-size contrast, its interval, the complete floor decomposition, the claim-side bound, the effect-to-floor ratio, and the final resolvable/unresolved verdict. No demonstration energy value from the superseded mint is carried into this draft. A quantization ladder will be included only if it is collected under its own stack-specific floors and the frozen window budget permits it.
2453:The Illusion of Power Capping in LLM Decode samples graphics-processor power, integrates those samples, repeats configurations, and cross-checks sufficiently long operations against a separate hardware energy counter [IllusionPowerCapping]. This is a stronger measurement template than an unqualified software reading. Its counter agreement, run-to-run variation, snapshot fallback, and timing alignment nevertheless remain separate diagnostics rather than one bound on the reported effect, and its long sweeps do not use a drift-control ordering. JouleWise composes those classes of uncertainty into a decision rule for each contrast.
2459:RAPL in Action established a validation agenda for commodity software counters: align lag before comparing streams, model wall power rather than assuming identity, account for temporal correlation, warm the system, measure sampler overhead, and inspect update granularity, overflow, jitter, and timestamp behavior [RAPLInAction]. Jay and Ostapenco likewise regress software readings against wall power and show that disagreement varies with load; they avoid claims about subtotals that the reference meter cannot observe [JayOstapenco]. JouleWise follows this epistemic boundary. A future external meter could test total gain and load dependence, but it would not validate how a total is divided between prefill and decode. The in-window pulse train addresses that distinct question.
2467:This emphasis changes the role of failed runs. A rejected admission, stale calibration, contaminated member, or below-floor contrast is evidence about the instrument's operating domain. Hash-bound raw traces, runtime events, configurations, supersessions, verdicts, and pre-registration records make that evidence re-reducible. The refusal is retained rather than disappearing behind a final average.

./env/README.md:47:`mac = ["mlx-lm>=0.31.3", "transformers<5.13"]`). The lockfiles are
./env/README.md-48-*reconstruction* specs, used as pip **constraints**, never as a parallel
./env/README.md-49-dependency list:
./env/README.md-50-
./env/README.md-51-```sh

./docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/reviews/rev-long-generation-dynamics.md-99-**F3 — Duplicative of banked work whose discipline it doesn't cite, and it picks the weaker
./docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/reviews/rev-long-generation-dynamics.md-100-of two designs that cost the same nights.** `docs/research_question_registry.md:48` banks
./docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/reviews/rev-long-generation-dynamics.md-101-**RQ-KV-GROWTH** at "L1/L2 chunked", "no per-token joule claims", with the rider "bounded-
./docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/reviews/rev-long-generation-dynamics.md-102-window KV marginal slope". **C5-2.12** (`research_question_bank.md:977`) already specifies
./docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/reviews/rev-long-generation-dynamics.md-103-the *interventional* version: bounded evicting `RotatingKVCache` via `max_kv_size` vs
./docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/reviews/rev-long-generation-dynamics.md:104:unbounded step-growing `KVCache` — available in the pinned mlx-lm, ABBA-counterbalanceable
./docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/reviews/rev-long-generation-dynamics.md-105-at matched positions, with a real alias null and a real comparative floor. The proposal
./docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/reviews/rev-long-generation-dynamics.md-106-defers this ("a causal KV-mechanism claim would still require a later bounded-versus-
./docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/reviews/rev-long-generation-dynamics.md-107-unbounded cache intervention") while spending the same nights on the confounded version.
./docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/reviews/rev-long-generation-dynamics.md-108-That is a design error, not a scoping choice.

· commit dbd8137"><span class="source-file">docs/<wbr>risk_register.md</span><span class="source-commit">commit dbd8137</span></span></div> <!-- rendered: marked@18.0.6 --> <h1>Risk Register</h1> <p>Living register of risks that could sink, delay, or weaken the capstone. Review at the start of every phase and whenever a trigger fires; update statuses at the end of substantial runs alongside <code>RUN_STATE.md</code>.</p> <p>Conventions:</p> <ul> <li>Likelihood/Impact: low / medium / high, judged against the current phase.</li> <li>Trigger: the observable event that means the risk is materializing.</li> <li>Mitigation: what we do <em>now</em> to reduce likelihood or impact.</li> <li>Fallback: what we do <em>if it happens</em> - every fallback must preserve a publishable result, even if smaller.</li> <li>Owner: <code>user</code> for actions needing human/lab/supervisor access, <code>agent</code> for repo work.</li> </ul> <h2 id="summary">Summary</h2> <div class="table-scroll"><table> <thead> <tr> <th>ID</th> <th>Risk</th> <th>Phase</th> guardrails)</td> </tr> </tbody></table></div> <h2 id="r-001-supervisor-approval-delayed-or-scope-shifts">R-001: Supervisor approval delayed or scope shifts</h2> <ul> <li>Phase: 1. Likelihood: medium. Impact: high (wrong deliverable built).</li> <li>Trigger: Phase 2 implementation slices ready to start (2A-2F complete) with P1-001 still open; or any supervisor communication contradicting <code>AGENT_PLAN.md</code> scope.</li> <li>Status note (2026-07-05): the first trigger fired 2026-06-12 (2A-2F completed with P1-001 still open). The mitigation is holding as designed - all work since has been hardware-independent and harness-shaped (mock slice, docs, Slice 2N is next and is also ungated) - and the fallback (&quot;continue only mock/local work; hardware purchases/borrows blocked-on-approval&quot;) is effectively in force.</li> <li>Mitigation: the queue keeps P1-001 ranked first; all work until approval stays hardware-independent and harness-shaped (valuable under any scope); the Phase 1 exit checklist lists the exact questions to put to the supervisor so one meeting can close the gate.</li> <li>Fallback: if approval stalls past mock-slice completion, continue only mock/local work and mark every hardware purchase or borrow decision blocked-on-approval.</li> <li>Owner: user.</li> </ul> <h2 id="r-002-powermetrics-sudo-workflow-not-approved-on-measurement-mac">R-002: powermetrics sudo workflow not approved on measurement Mac</h2> <ul> <li>Phase: 2. Likelihood: low (user controls the machine; a local auth session needs rescheduling - the planned 2026-06-10 slot passed without one). Impact: high (no Mac telemetry = no flagship vertical slice).</li> <li>Status: closed-residual (2026-07-08). The working Mac slice completed 2G/2H/2I on 2026-07-06 with privileged powermetrics capture and strict-valid bundles; revisit for new macOS/MLX/powermetrics versions or new Mac hardware.</li> <li>Trigger: scoped sudoers rule (D-004) cannot be installed, or privileged sample capture fails after the auth session.</li> <li>Mitigation: D-004 defines a minimal, single-binary sudoers rule with the exact line documented in the Phase 1 exit checklist&#39;s instrumentation section; interactive-sudo manual fallback documented for attended runs.</li> <li>Fallback: attended runs with interactive sudo (operator present per experiment); if even that is unacceptable, the Mac becomes runtime-supported/telemetry-blocked and the first real slice moves to the first available CUDA target - recorded as a finding, not hidden.</li> <li>Owner: user (install rule), agent (pre-check + structured failure).</li> </ul> <h2 id="r-003-mlx-install-or-model-load-failure-on-mac">R-003: MLX install or model-load failure on Mac</h2> <ul> <li>Phase: 2. Likelihood: low. Impact: medium (delays flagship slice).</li> <li>Status: closed-residual (2026-07-08). The working Mac slice completed 2G/2H/2I on 2026-07-06 with MLX generation and strict-valid bundles; revisit for new MLX/mlx-lm versions or new Mac hardware.</li> <li>Trigger: <code>pip install mlx mlx-lm</code> fails, or the chosen model (D-016) has no working MLX artifact.</li> <li>Mitigation: install into a dedicated venv with versions recorded in run bundles; model criteria (D-016) require known MLX availability before selection; smoke-test load before scheduling measurement sessions.</li> <li>Fallback: llama.cpp with the Metal backend as the Mac runtime (already a planned runtime for split portability under D-015); the MLX adapter then becomes optional rather than flagship.</li> <li>Owner: agent (with user approving installs).</li> </ul> <h2 id="r-004-kv-persist-resume-unsupported-in-a-target-runtime">R-004: KV persist/resume unsupported in a target runtime</h2> <ul> <li>Phase: 3. Likelihood: medium overall (high for vLLM file-based replay, low for llama.cpp, low-medium for mlx-lm). Impact: high if unmitigated - this is the project&#39;s central feasibility risk.</li> <li>Trigger: a Stage 3.0 spike returns <code>replay_unsupported</code> for a runtime needed by a planned pairing.</li> <li>Mitigation: D-015&#39;s feasibility ladder - spikes run <em>before</em> any split hardware time is scheduled; pairings are planned only on runtimes with <code>replay_supported</code> verdicts; the synthetic transfer microbenchmark (Stage 3.1) is independent of all runtime cooperation and guarantees a crossover dataset.</li> <li>Fallback: analytical composition - measured prefill energy (node A) + measured synthetic transfer energy (payload sized by the KV model) + measured decode energy (node B) bounds the split cost honestly; the report states the composition method explicitly.</li> <li>Owner: agent.</li> </ul> <h2 id="r-005-llama-cpp-cache-files-not-portable-across-machines-backends">R-005: llama.cpp cache files not portable across machines/backends</h2> <ul> <li>Phase: 3. Likelihood: medium (session files are version- and model-sensitive; cross-backend CUDA-save -&gt; Metal-load is unverified). Impact: high for <em>heterogeneous</em> pairings specifically.</li> <li>Trigger: Stage 3.0.2&#39;s cross-machine restore test fails or produces divergent output.</li> <li>Mitigation: the spike tests cross-machine restore explicitly, with pinned identical llama.cpp versions and identical GGUF files on both ends, before any heterogeneous experiment is scheduled.</li> <li>Fallback: restrict offline-replay pairings to same-platform pairs (GPU-&gt;GPU in the borrow window, Orin-&gt;Orin); cover heterogeneous pairs with the analytical composition (R-004 fallback); report the portability finding itself - it is a legitimate disaggregation-practicality result.</li> <li>Owner: agent.</li> </ul> <h2 id="r-006-3080-ti-borrow-window-slips-or-shrinks">R-006: 3080 Ti borrow window slips or shrinks</h2> <ul> <li>Phase: 3. Likelihood: medium. Impact: medium (loses GPU-&gt;GPU pairing, not the phase).</li> <li>Trigger: window not scheduled by Phase 3 Stage 3.2 completion; or window arrives before split tooling is ready.</li> <li>Mitigation: all split tooling reaches rehearsed-on-available-hardware state before the window (the Phase 3 plan keeps a borrow-window runbook so borrow time is execution-only, no debugging); calendar mapping task (P1-008) makes the window a tracked date.</li> <li>Fallback: GPU-&gt;GPU pairing drops to single-GPU prefill/decode phase decomposition plus analytical composition; 3050&lt;-&gt;Orin and Orin&lt;-&gt;Orin remain.</li> <li>Owner: user (scheduling), agent (runbook readiness).</li> </ul> <h2 id="r-007-no-wall-meter-available">R-007: No wall meter available</h2> <ul> <li>Phase: 1-4. Likelihood: medium. Impact: medium (boundary calibration and Pi/Hailo coverage lost; per-target results stand).</li> <li>Trigger: P1-003 resolves &quot;unavailable&quot;.</li> <li>Mitigation: P1-003 is a Phase 1 gate precisely so this resolves before it matters; D-018&#39;s boundary table makes results honest without a meter.</li> <li>Fallback: report within-target comparisons (always boundary-consistent) as primary; flag cross-target absolute comparisons with the boundary caveat; targets with no platform telemetry (Pi) become telemetry-unavailable findings.</li> <li>Owner: user.</li> </ul> <h2 id="r-008-orin-telemetry-inaccessible">R-008: Orin telemetry inaccessible</h2> <ul> <li>Phase: 2-3. Likelihood: medium (rail sysfs paths vary by L4T version). Impact: low (one target of several).</li> <li>Trigger: P1-006 evidence shows neither INA3221 sysfs nor tegrastats usable.</li> <li>Mitigation: two candidate mechanisms documented before hardware time; wall-meter fallback if R-007 resolves positively.</li> <li>Fallback: Orin runs runtime-only (latency/throughput) marked telemetry-unavailable, or drops to a stretch target.</li> <li>Owner: user (access), agent (adapter).</li> </ul> <h2 id="r-009-hailo-cannot-run-llm-shaped-workloads">R-009: Hailo cannot run LLM-shaped workloads</h2> <ul> <li>Phase: 1. Likelihood: high. Impact: low - <em>by design</em>: the plan treats Hailo as a feasibility investigation whose negative verdict is itself a reportable applicability finding.</li> <li>Status: <strong>realized as expected, 2026-06-12</strong> — verdict <code>unsupported_workload</code>. The trigger fired (a non-<code>supported</code> verdict), the by-design mitigation held, and the outcome is the publishable applicability finding the plan anticipated. No schedule impact.</li> <li>Trigger: feasibility checklist closes with any non-<code>supported</code> verdict. (Fired 2026-06-12.)</li> <li>Mitigation: none needed; the verdict-code structure in the Phase 1 exit checklist&#39;s Hailo section makes the outcome publishable either way. Do not spend implementation effort on a Hailo backend (the verdict is now recorded; the standing do-not-do-yet rule becomes &quot;report, don&#39;t implement&quot;).</li> <li>Fallback: Pi 5 CPU-only llama.cpp with wall-meter telemetry becomes an optional low-power data point if the meter exists; otherwise Pi/Hailo appears only in the applicability table.</li> <li>Owner: user (device access), agent (verdict documentation - done).</li> </ul> <h2 id="r-010-controller-as-dut-contamination-on-mac-runs">R-010: Controller-as-DUT contamination on Mac runs</h2> <ul> <li>Phase: 2. Likelihood: high if unmitigated. Impact: medium (biased flagship numbers).</li> <li>Status: mitigated by D-013 (idle baseline includes resident quiescent controller; deferred logging; blocking wait during measured window).</li> <li>Trigger (residual): SSH-controlled comparison runs (once transport exists) show a delta beyond run-to-run variance.</li> <li>Fallback: move Mac headline measurements to remote-controlled runs.</li> <li>Owner: agent.</li> </ul> <h2 id="r-011-benchmark-network-cannot-be-isolated">R-011: Benchmark network cannot be isolated</h2> <ul> <li>Phase: 3. Likelihood: medium (campus/home network constraints unknown until P1-004 closes). Impact: medium (noisy transfer measurements).</li> <li>Trigger: P1-004 topology answer shows shared links only.</li> <li>Mitigation: prefer direct node-to-node cabling (no switch) for 1GbE/2.5GbE point-to-point tests - removes the isolation question entirely for two-node experiments; record link conditions per run in the bundle.</li> <li>Fallback: run sweeps off-hours, repeat n&gt;=5, report observed throughput alongside nominal link speed (the bundle already records measured throughput per D-008&#39;s transfer block).</li> <li>Owner: user (hardware), agent (recording).</li> </ul> <h2 id="r-012-schedule-five-phases-vs-fixed-academic-deadlines">R-012: Schedule: five phases vs fixed academic deadlines</h2> <ul> <li>Phase: all. Likelihood: medium. Impact: high (capstones fail by calendar, not by code).</li> <li>Trigger: any phase exceeding its (to-be-set) calendar budget; colloquium or report dates announced (P1-008) leaving less runway than the plan assumes.</li> <li>Mitigation: P1-008 maps phases to real dates as soon as the user supplies them (<code>docs/milestones.md</code> holds the skeleton); every phase defines a hardware-independent floor and a descope ladder so cutting is a decision, not a scramble.</li> <li>Descope ladder (worst-case minimum viable capstone, in cut order):<ol> <li>Drop live split (3.3) - already stretch.</li> <li>Drop 10GbE and one model size.</li> <li>Drop heterogeneous replay pairs (keep synthetic transfer + analytical composition).</li> <li>Drop Orin/Pi targets (keep Mac + one CUDA).</li> <li>Floor: mock harness + Mac vertical slice + homogeneous baselines + synthetic interconnect sweep + analytical split model. This is still a complete, defensible benchmark-plus-study.</li> </ol> </li> <li>Owner: user (dates), agent (floor discipline).</li> </ul> <h2 id="r-013-thermal-throttling-confounds-measurements">R-013: Thermal throttling confounds measurements</h2> <ul> <li>Phase: 2-4. Likelihood: medium (high on passively-cooled Orin/Pi). Impact: medium (rep-to-rep drift, biased late reps).</li> <li>Status: mitigated by D-014 (idle-power recovery gate between reps, thermal_drift_c in measurement quality, interleaved ordering) - residual risk on targets without thermal sensors.</li> <li>Trigger: thermal_drift_c trending across reps, or cooldown cap hits recorded in bundles.</li> <li>Fallback: longer cooldowns, active cooling notes recorded in run metadata, or excluding throttled reps <em>with documented cause</em> per D-014.</li> <li>Owner: agent.</li> </ul> <h2 id="r-014-model-weights-become-unavailable-or-gated">R-014: Model weights become unavailable or gated</h2> <ul> <li>Phase: 2+. Likelihood: low. Impact: medium (mid-project model swap breaks comparability).</li> <li>Trigger: chosen model&#39;s hub entry gated/removed; license terms change.</li> <li>Mitigation: D-016 requires mirroring chosen weights to local storage immediately on selection, with revisions and hashes recorded.</li> <li>Fallback: promote the recorded fallback candidate; re-run affected baselines (the config hash separates old/new data cleanly).</li> <li>Owner: agent.</li> </ul> <h2 id="r-015-schema-changes-after-data-collection-starts">R-015: Schema changes after data collection starts</h2> <ul> <li>Phase: 2+. Likelihood: low. Impact: high (existing bundles unreadable or silently misread).</li> <li>Status: mitigated structurally.</li> <li>Mitigation: schema_version field exists from v0.1; D-008 plans the only anticipated breaking-shape change (v0.2) <em>before</em> split data collection; output-schema additions are additive-only (the JSON schema does not forbid additional properties); <code>validate-bundle</code> pins what a valid bundle means per version.</li> <li>Trigger: any proposed non-additive change to a schema with bundles already on disk.</li> <li>Fallback: a dated migration note in this repo plus a one-shot migration script; never edit bundles in place (they are evidence).</li> <li>Owner: agent.</li> </ul> <h2 id="r-016-measurement-corpus-loss-runs-has-no-backup-path">R-016: Measurement-corpus loss (runs/ has no backup path)</h2> <ul> <li>Phase: 2-5. Likelihood: low. Impact: high (the dataset behind every claim is a gitignored directory on one disk; a disk failure or an errant delete erases the evidence the defense rests on, and hardware re-collection needs access windows that may not recur).</li> <li>Trigger: first real (non-mock) bundle written; any data-affecting incident (disk error, iCloud eviction anomaly, accidental delete).</li> <li>Mitigation: before the first real measurement session (gate on 2I data collection, tracked as queue task P0-002), define and record the backup protocol here: destination (external disk and/or cloud location outside the repo), cadence (after every measurement session), method (rsync of <code>runs/</code> plus experiment manifests), and a restore test performed once. Configs + manifests already make re-collection well-defined; backups make it unnecessary.</li> <li><strong>Protocol recorded (2026-07-06, P0-002 closed interim).</strong> Destination: <code>~/JouleWise-backup</code> — a user-directed INTERIM location on the same disk (&quot;cursory... I&#39;ll handle that later&quot;); it protects against errant deletes but not disk failure, so the user still owes an external/cloud destination for full mitigation. Cadence: after every measurement session. Method: <code>scripts/backup_runs.sh [RUNS_DIR] [DEST]</code> (rsync -a, never <code>--delete</code>; dated UTC log line per invocation appended to <code>DEST/backup.log</code>). Restore test performed 2026-07-06: mock bundle backed up, restored to a temp dir, <code>validate-bundle</code> green on the restored copy. Swapping in the final destination is a one-argument change (or edit the script default) plus one fresh restore test.</li> <li><strong>Protocol upgraded (2026-07-10/11, P0-003 closed; addendum 2026-07-16 closing a summary-row/body drift found by the resumption audit).</strong> The interim same-disk destination above is superseded: the external destination is iCloud Drive, live with a fresh backup + restore test passed (evidence: <code>docs/run_reports/2026-07-11-c028-continuation.md</code> §11, &quot;The P0-003 iCloud measurement-corpus backup and restore gate is satisfied&quot;). The 2026-07-06 entry above is retained as history. Standing caveat: iCloud eviction — re-verify the destination is materialized (fresh restore test) before each measurement window.</li> <li>Fallback: re-run affected experiments from their configs (the config hash separates old/new data cleanly per D-005/D-010); report any unrecoverable gap honestly in the exclusion log.</li> <li>Owner: user (destination/media), agent (protocol doc + restore test).</li> </ul> <h2 id="r-017-repo-lives-on-icloud-synced-desktop-eperm-lock-recurrence">R-017: Repo lives on iCloud-synced Desktop (EPERM lock recurrence)</h2> <ul> <li>Phase: all. Likelihood: low (mitigated; was high while on Desktop). Impact: medium (blocks work sessions mid-run; small integrity risk around eviction during writes).</li> <li>Status: <strong>mitigated 2026-07-05</strong> - the repo moved off the synced Desktop (current canonical path: <code>~/code/JouleWise</code>; the interim <code>~/code/CapstoneRivoire/Capstone</code> path recorded here was itself later renamed - corrected 2026-07-09, C-027). P0-001 complete; git + suite verified green at the new path. Residual exposure: agent sessions launched from the stale Desktop path (delete the leftover <code>~/Desktop/CapstoneRivoire</code> husk after relaunching from the new path), and any future placement of repo or <code>runs/</code> data under an iCloud-synced directory - do not.</li> <li>Trigger: any <code>Operation not permitted</code> on read/readdir inside the repo with the iCloud file provider (<code>bird</code>) active.</li> <li>History: first incident 2026-06-12 (documented in <code>RUN_STATE.md</code>); recurred 2026-07-05 mid-run - <code>docs/</code>, <code>joulewise/</code>, <code>tests/</code>, <code>.git</code>, and the repo root EPERM-locked intermittently during an active iCloud full-sync, clearing and re-locking per subtree. Both incidents match iCloud &quot;Optimize Mac Storage&quot; behavior on <code>~/Desktop/</code>. The move landed the same day as the second incident.</li> <li>Fallback: if a lock ever strikes again, wait for it to clear (both incidents did), then re-verify with the test suite before continuing; the remote (<code>origin/main</code>) bounds code loss to the working tree.</li> <li>Owner: user (launch paths), agent (post-lock verification discipline).</li> </ul> <h2 id="r-018-the-agent-loop-itself-as-a-schedule-and-scope-risk">R-018: The agent loop itself as a schedule and scope risk</h2> <ul> <li>Phase: all. Likelihood: medium. Impact: high (capstones fail by calendar, R-012).</li> <li>Registered by C-027 (NEGSPACE lens finding accepted in council): the multi-agent workflow can remain locally productive - packs, registries, meta-process, site work - while the graded deliverable path (rubric, report source, backup, real corpus, figures) stays starved. Same-day evidence at registration: ~6M tokens of breadth work vs six real corpus bundles, no report source, same-disk backup.</li> <li>Trigger: an agent-heavy work block that produces neither a new real evidence bundle nor a report/figure increment.</li> <li>Mitigation: D-060 depth-before-breadth stop line (RATIFIED by Ed 2026-07-10) extended by the WO-022/R2 spend guardrails (<code>docs/orchestration.md</code> §Spend guardrails, 2026-07-15); RPT-001 vertical slice; the C-027 correctness rows ranked ahead of all breadth work.</li> <li>Owner: lead (queue discipline + guardrail checkpoints), Ed (HARD bands and structure).</li> </ul> </div> </div> </main> <footer class="site"> <div class="inner"> <span>JouleWise · github.com/mpmdw/JouleWise</span> <span>docs/risk_register.md · commit dbd8137 · regenerate: <span class="mono">python3 scripts/build_site.py</span></span> </div> </footer> </body> </html>
--

of contents</div><a href="#measurement-principle">Measurement Principle</a> <a href="#run-lifecycle">Run Lifecycle</a> <a href="#idle-subtraction">Idle Subtraction</a> <a href="#thermal-state">Thermal And Multi-Node Alignment</a> <a href="#controller-co-residency-controller-as-dut">Controller Co-Residency (Controller-As-DUT)</a> <a href="#repetition-ordering-and-thermal-equilibrium">Repetition, class="doc-meta"><a href="library.html">Back to sources</a> · rendered from <code>docs/contracts/measurement_methodology.md</code></p> <div class="provenance-plate"><span class="source-chip" title="docs/contracts/measurement_methodology.md · commit 6d80039"><span class="source-file">docs/<wbr>contracts/<wbr>measurement_methodology.md</span><span class="source-commit">commit 6d80039</span></span></div> <!-- rendered: marked@18.0.6 --> <h1>Measurement Methodology</h1> <p>Living cross-phase contract, drafted in Phase 1. Changes require a decision-log entry when they bind later work.</p> <h2 id="measurement-principle">Measurement Principle</h2> <p>Every benchmark run must be reproducible from its raw artifacts. Summary metrics are derived outputs, not the source of truth.</p> <p>The source of truth for a run is the run bundle:</p> <ul> <li>Experiment config.</li> <li>Device and environment metadata.</li> <li>Event log with phase timestamps.</li> <li>Raw power trace.</li> <li>Raw model output.</li> <li>Reducer output.</li> <li>Runtime and telemetry logs.</li> </ul> <h2 id="run-lifecycle">Run Lifecycle</h2> <p>Before a campaign creates a run bundle, the operator runs the read-only doctor preflight described in <code>docs/contracts/doctor_preflight.md</code>. Schema-0.1 parsing continues to warn-and-ignore unknown keys for compatibility, but campaign execution fails before the first bundle when those warnings have not been explicitly acknowledged. The terminal campaign-verdict JSONL row records the exact warning set and acknowledgement; acknowledgement does not alter config bytes, collection evidence, claim readiness, or claim outcomes.</p> <p>Doctor also exposes architecture/version, configured model and tokenizer identity, requested sampler fields, inspect-only powermetrics privilege policy, thermal pressure, backup capacity, and quiet-machine warnings. These are preflight observations, not substitutes for per-bundle provenance or live measurement gates. In particular, doctor never starts powermetrics and never certifies that a machine is quiet.</p> <h3>Environment guard and per-run admission (D-077)</h3> <p>Campaigns select a strictly typed policy sidecar. <code>run_campaign.py</code> defaults to <code>configs/campaign_policies/quiet_mac_p2_production.json</code>, records the policy version and exact source-byte SHA-256 in campaign provenance and every member bundle, acquires the campaign lock, and only then performs the enforcing environment preflight before member 1. The production quiet-Mac guard requires AC power and an externally connected power source, low-power mode off, all online displays asleep, the screensaver disengaged, and Nominal thermal pressure. Unknown critical probes fail closed. Load averages are recorded as preflight evidence only and never gate a member.</p> <p>Default operation is verify-only. <code>--arm-quiet-mode</code> is an explicit transient operation: the runner displays a countdown, requests <code>pmset displaysleepnow</code>, and repeats the complete environment probe before deciding admission. It does not write display-sleep, screensaver, or other persistent host settings. An operator override is accepted only when its JSON binds the exact failed snapshot and findings SHA-256 values and records a reason, approver, and timestamp. It is stored as an <code>override</code>, not a waiver, and universally bars all resulting members from gross-energy, idle-subtracted-energy, and throughput claims.</p> <p>At each governed member&#39;s idle-baseline stage, the controller captures the same critical environment evidence and verifies that the display remains asleep and the screensaver remains disengaged. Awake, engaged, or unknown state aborts immediately. The first idle baseline is admitted only when the existing powermetrics GPU-idle-quality classification records <code>idle_window_suspect == false</code>. One and only one complete retry is allowed; both attempts preserve distinct raw artifacts and provenance. A persistent failure either aborts (production) or records the exploratory-only, unwaivable <code>environment_admission_failed</code> claim barrier (<code>on_fail: flag</code>). There is no skip disposition in a fixed-n campaign. A lightweight post-run display/screensaver/HID observation makes within-member transitions visible.</p> <p>The sidecar is deliberately separate from <code>BenchmarkConfig</code>. Direct <code>joulewise run</code> without a sidecar retains legacy flag-only/non-enforcing behavior, and omission of the additive policy/admission metadata preserves legacy normalized config serialization and hashes.</p> <h3>Per-bundle source provenance</h3> <p><code>RunBundleWriter.create</code> captures the harness source state before it creates bundle artifacts or returns control to any adapter. <code>write_metadata</code> captures the end state after adapter execution. <code>metadata.git_commit</code> remains the creation-time commit for compatibility; the governed record is <code>metadata.source_provenance</code> with schema <code>joulewise.source_provenance.v1</code>.</p> <p>Each <code>start</code> and <code>end</code> snapshot records <code>git_commit</code>, <code>tracked</code>, <code>staged</code>, <code>untracked</code>, and <code>diff_sha256</code>. The three state values are independently:</p> <ul> <li><code>clean</code>: the corresponding Git probe succeeded and found no change;</li> <li><code>dirty</code>: an unstaged tracked diff, staged diff, or non-ignored untracked path was present, respectively; or</li> <li><code>unknown</code>: the corresponding probe or required file read failed. Failure is never interpreted as clean.</li> </ul> <p>The privacy-safe diff identity descriptor is <code>sha256</code> / <code>joulewise.git-diff.nul-v1</code>. The producer captures the byte output of <code>git diff --no-ext-diff --no-textconv --binary</code>, the analogous <code>--cached</code> command, and <code>git ls-files --others --exclude-standard -z</code>. For each sorted untracked path it hashes, without serializing, the NUL-safe length-framed path, file kind, mode, size, and SHA-256 of regular-file bytes or symlink-target bytes. The final identity is SHA-256 over the version plus length-framed <code>tracked</code>, <code>staged</code>, and untracked-inventory byte identities. Bundles contain only the final digest and state labels: never a diff, path, untracked file content, or secret.</p> <p><code>changed_during_run</code> is true when two fully known snapshots differ, false when they match, and null when either snapshot is not fully known. <code>claim_eligible</code> is true only when both commits and diff identities are known, all six component states are clean, and the snapshots match. <code>reason_codes</code> is the deterministic list of every start/end unknown or dirty component followed, when applicable, by <code>source_changed_during_run</code>. Bundle completion remains allowed in every state so raw evidence is not discarded.</p> <p>Dirty, unknown, changed, missing, or internally inconsistent provenance is a hard exclusion for claim-bearing use. The publication pack preflight enforces that boundary and refuses such bundles. Analysis-side admission propagation is separate from capture and field semantics and is owned by WO-004/T11.</p> <ol> <li>Validate config.</li> <li>Create run directory.</li> <li>Collect device metadata.</li> <li>Measure idle baseline.</li> <li>Warm up runtime.</li> <li>Wait the configured post-warmup settling interval (<code>sampling.warmup_seconds</code>; zero means no wait).</li> <li>Start measured telemetry.</li> <li>Run workload.</li> <li>Stop measured telemetry.</li> <li>Cleanup runtime.</li> <li>Reduce raw artifacts into summary metrics.</li> </ol> <p>The post-warmup settling interval begins only after all active <code>workload_profile.warmup_runs</code> calls and their clock-alignment captures have completed. It ends before the measured-run stage and sampling-active markers, so it is never integrated into the measured window. Controller events record the configured value on the warmup completion event and the runtime log records positive waits.</p> <h2 id="idle-subtraction">Idle Subtraction</h2> <p>Energy metrics must report both gross and idle-subtracted values when possible. The idle baseline is measured before each run and stored in the run bundle.</p> <p>Minimum idle fields:</p> <ul> <li><code>idle_power_w_mean</code></li> <li><code>idle_power_w_stddev</code></li> <li><code>idle_duration_s</code></li> <li><code>idle_sample_count</code></li> <li><code>telemetry_backend</code></li> </ul> <h2 id="thermal-state">Thermal State</h2> <p>Each telemetry backend should report thermal state before and after measured runs when the platform exposes it.</p> <p>Minimum thermal fields:</p> <ul> <li><code>temperature_c</code></li> <li><code>thermal_pressure</code> or platform equivalent, when available.</li> <li><code>fan_state</code> or cooling mode, when available.</li> </ul> <h2 id="uncertainty">Uncertainty</h2> <p>Phase 1 defines uncertainty fields; Phase 2 implements reducer behavior. Repeated runs should report:</p> <ul> <li>Number of repetitions.</li> <li>Mean.</li> <li>Standard deviation.</li> <li>Confidence interval method.</li> <li>Confidence interval bounds.</li> </ul> <h2 id="measurement-quality-fields">Measurement Quality Fields</h2> <p>Each run summary should include:</p> <ul> <li>Sampling rate requested.</li> <li>Sampling rate observed.</li> <li>Dropped or malformed samples.</li> <li>Idle variance.</li> <li>Thermal drift.</li> <li>Telemetry source.</li> <li>Local runtime cleanup result (<code>runtime_cleanup_ok</code>: true/false/null). Cleanup occurs after the measured window, so failure is a quality concern for the following repetition and does not retroactively change current-run status or energy.</li> <li>Wall-meter comparison delta, when available.</li> </ul> <h2 id="phase-labels">Phase Labels</h2> <p>The event log should use stable phase names:</p> <ul> <li><code>idle</code></li> <li><code>warmup</code></li> <li><code>prefill</code></li> <li><code>decode</code></li> <li><code>serialize</code></li> <li><code>transfer</code></li> <li><code>deserialize</code></li> <li><code>cleanup</code></li> <li><code>failure</code></li> </ul> <p><code>deserialize</code> (cache load on the decode node) was added 2026-06-09 alongside the split-run accounting definitions (see <code>docs/phase_3/phase_3_plan.md</code>); phase labels are strings in the schema, so the addition is non-breaking. Split-stage accounting, pinned so reducers and prose agree: serialize = cache-persist window on the prefill node; transfer = byte-movement window; deserialize = cache-load window on the decode node; decode = first-token to last-token. Cache load is not decode energy.</p> <h2 id="hardware-classification">Hardware Classification</h2> <p>Every target should end Phase 1 in one state:</p> <ul> <li><code>supported</code>: known viable and ready for Phase 2 implementation.</li> <li><code>pending</code>: expected viable but not fully checked.</li> <li><code>unsupported</code>: not viable for a documented technical reason.</li> </ul> <h2 id="measurement-boundaries">Measurement Boundaries</h2> <p>&quot;Power&quot; means a different physical boundary on each telemetry backend. Cross-target absolute comparisons must state the boundary difference; the final report&#39;s limitations section inherits this table. Decision D-018 defines the rail policy (per-rail trace rows plus a per-backend rail manifest naming the canonical sum).</p> <div class="table-scroll"><table> <thead> <tr> <th>Backend</th> <th>Boundary</th> <th>Included</th> <th>Excluded</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody><tr> <td>powermetrics</td> <td>Apple SoC subsystems</td> <td>CPU + GPU + ANE package power</td> <td>display, storage, memory at wall, PSU losses</td> </tr> <tr> <td>nvidia_smi</td> <td>GPU board</td> <td>board power as reported by driver</td> <td>host CPU, DRAM, motherboard, PSU losses</td> </tr> <tr> <td>jetson_rails</td> <td>module input (VDD_IN preferred; actual rail recorded)</td> <td>module power</td> <td>carrier-board peripherals (rail-dependent), PSU losses</td> </tr> <tr> <td>wall_meter</td> <td>full system AC</td> <td>everything incl. PSU losses</td> <td>nothing</td> </tr> <tr> <td>mock</td> <td>synthetic</td> <td>n/a</td> <td>n/a</td> </tr> </tbody></table></div> <p>Rules:</p> <ul> <li>Within-target comparisons (the same backend) are always boundary-consistent and are the primary claim type.</li> <li>Cross-target comparisons are reported with boundaries named; where the wall meter exists, the wall-vs-platform delta is recorded per target and used to contextualize the gap.</li> <li>Each telemetry adapter declares its rail manifest in <code>device_metadata</code>; the reducer sums exactly the manifest rails to produce <code>power_w</code>.</li> </ul> <h2 id="clock-synchronization-and-multi-node-alignment">Clock Synchronization And Multi-Node Alignment</h2> <p>Policy per decision D-003:</p> <ul> <li>Canonical <code>timestamp_s</code> everywhere is epoch UTC from <code>time.time()</code> via the injected clock; no other time base appears in artifacts.</li> <li>Each process records its monotonic-vs-wall offset at start in metadata (detects wall-clock steps mid-run).</li> <li>Each node records NTP sync state in metadata when determinable.</li> <li>For multi-node runs, the controller bounds per-node clock offset with marker events: timestamp a no-op command on the remote node immediately before and after each remote stage; half the round trip bounds the offset. The bound is recorded in composite-bundle metadata.</li> <li>Reducers must flag (in measurement quality) any cross-node interval shorter than the recorded offset bound; such intervals are not used for energy attribution claims.</li> <li>Required precision: at 1-10 Hz power sampling, tens of milliseconds - comfortably within LAN NTP plus the marker bound.</li> </ul> <h2 id="controller-co-residency-controller-as-dut">Controller Co-Residency (Controller-As-DUT)</h2> <p>On Mac-local runs the controller process runs on the measured machine. Mitigation per decision D-013:</p> <ul> <li>The idle baseline is measured with the controller resident and quiescent, so the controller&#39;s floor load is included in what idle subtraction removes.</li> <li>During the measured window the controller only blocks on the runtime: no logging, no polling, no file writes; log records buffer in memory and flush after sampling stops.</li> <li>Residual risk is recorded, not hidden: OS background activity affects idle and measured windows alike; the upgrade path (remote-controlled Mac runs once the SSH transport exists) is queued as a validation comparison.</li> </ul> <h2 id="repetition-ordering-and-thermal-equilibrium">Repetition, Ordering, And Thermal Equilibrium</h2> <p>Per decisions D-005 and D-014:</p> <ul> <li>Each repetition is an independent run bundle; an experiment manifest groups members and records the executed order.</li> <li>Between live repetitions, cooldown v2 holds until the retained evidence has both a complete 30-second wall-clock span and at least <code>coverage_fraction * sustained_window_s</code> of captured coverage (<code>coverage_fraction = 0.8</code> by default), and its duration-weighted idle-power mean satisfies the one-sided rule <code>rolling_mean &lt;= reference * (1 + tolerance)</code> (10% by the production policy), while thermal pressure is Nominal. A below-reference mean therefore counts as recovery. An optional calibrated absolute ceiling is an additional upper cap and never an OR escape. The wait has a 5-minute cap; the cap is evaluated before release on every iteration, so recovery criteria first met at or after the deadline remain a <code>cap_hit</code> (with the late criteria recorded in the trace) and are recorded in the following repetition&#39;s measurement quality.</li> <li>The preceding baseline is eligible as a cooldown reference only when <code>idle_window_suspect == false</code>, all critical environment probes passed, and policy/environment provenance is present. An ineligible or unknown reference falls back to one frozen clean anchor: the NEG-8 reference start when present, otherwise the first admission-passing baseline. The anchor&#39;s source and hashes are recorded and it is never updated from later outcomes. With neither an eligible reference nor an anchor the gate fails closed. The following member records policy version, eligibility decision, anchor provenance, thresholds (including <code>coverage_fraction</code>), wall-clock span, required and observed coverage, thermal result, and the exact release criterion under <code>preceding_campaign_cooldown</code>. Historical recovered rows retain their recorded meaning and are not reinterpreted.</li> <li>Conditions are interleaved round-robin where model-reload cost permits; where blocks are operationally forced, the order is recorded so drift correlation can be audited (Phase 4 Stage 4.5 does this audit).</li> </ul> <h2 id="statistical-protocol">Statistical Protocol</h2> <p>Per decision D-014 (draft to be ratified against observed variance at Phase 4 Stage 4.0), amended 2026-07-09 (C-023 S3; amendments ratified by D-053):</p> <ul> <li>Repetitions: n &gt;= 5 for headline comparisons; n &gt;= 3 minimum elsewhere; the n is recorded per experiment.</li> <li>Intervals: report mean, sample standard deviation, and 95% confidence interval via Student t; Phase 4 runs a bootstrap sensitivity comparison and reports both where they materially disagree.</li> <li>Outliers: flagged by modified z-score on MAD &gt; 3.5; never silently dropped; reported with-and-without only when a physical cause is identified and documented; otherwise kept in headline numbers. Amendment 2026-07-09 (C-023 S3, ratified by D-053): at n &lt;= 10, reports also run a leave-one-out influence check on every claim-bearing contrast. The report lists the full-data estimate/CI/verdict and each leave-one-out estimate/CI/verdict. An omitted point is influential if it changes the sign, floor status, adjusted rejection/equivalence verdict, or moves the estimate by more than 0.25 x the active threshold: MDE for rank/MDE-gated claims, otherwise the floor gate. Influential points are reported as sensitivity evidence, not silently removed.</li> <li>Figures always show raw points alongside aggregates.</li> <li>Amendment 2026-07-09 (C-023 S3, ratified by D-053): differences are claimed from the confidence interval of the paired/block difference, or from the named model contrast, not by visual separation of marginal intervals. Where execution order was randomized, the analysis includes a permutation/randomization check for the same contrast following the actual randomization scheme, permuting labels only within exchangeable blocks/strata. The minimum for this check is 6 exchangeable blocks; below that count, report the check as not run and rely on the contrast CI with the caveat that randomization-inference sensitivity was underpowered. A paired contrast is preferred when it matches the design; mixed or hierarchical models are reserved for real dependence structures that a paired/block contrast cannot represent. Floor-gated outcomes use a three-way rule: below-floor contrasts are <code>not resolvable</code>; above-floor contrasts whose CI does not support direction are <code>unresolved</code> with no directional claim; equivalence or &quot;no difference&quot; language requires a predeclared equivalence gate whose margin exceeds the floor and whose contrast CI lies entirely within that margin.</li> </ul> </div> </div> </main> <footer class="site"> <div class="inner"> <span>JouleWise · github.com/mpmdw/JouleWise</span> <span>docs/contracts/measurement_methodology.md · commit 6d80039 · regenerate: <span class="mono">python3 scripts/build_site.py</span></span> </div> </footer> </body> </html>
