de665ea"><span class="source-file">TASK_QUEUE.md</span><span class="source-commit">commit de665ea</span></span></div> <!-- rendered: marked@18.0.6 --> <h1>JouleWise Task Queue</h1> <p>This is the live queue for JouleWise work. When the user gives a new task, first triage it here instead of assuming it should happen immediately.</p> <h2 id="intake-rule-for-new-tasks">Intake Rule For New Tasks</h2> <p>For every new user task:</p> <ol> <li>Read <code>RUN_STATE.md</code>.</li> <li>Read this file.</li> <li>Check <code>git status --short --branch</code>.</li> <li>Review the last 2-3 commits with <code>git log --oneline --decorate -3</code>.</li> <li>Check relevant handoffs in <code>docs/run_reports/</code>.</li> <li>If <code>RUN_STATE.md</code> contains an ACTIVE <code>ACTIVE_STOP_CARD</code>, that card outranks this queue. Execute or preserve the card&#39;s resume/cleanup instructions before considering any lower-ranked work.</li> <li>Decide whether the task is:<ul> <li>urgent workspace hygiene,</li> <li>Phase 1 evidence work,</li> <li>Phase 2 implementation prep,</li> <li>later-phase research work,</li> <li>documentation/reporting,</li> <li>or unrelated/new scope.</li> </ul> </li> <li>Place or update the task in the queue with priority, rationale, evidence, and blockers.</li> <li>If executing it now, say why it outranks the current top task.</li> <li>Closure rule (D-023): a row may move to Completed only after the corresponding phase exit-checklist matrix row already shows the same status with dated evidence, and the Completed row&#39;s evidence cell must cite that matrix row (file + item id). If no matrix row exists for the work, say so explicitly in the evidence cell.</li> </ol> <h2 id="priority-scale">Priority Scale</h2> <ul> <li><strong>P0 Safety</strong>: prevents accidental data loss, bad commits, broken handoffs, or corrupted repo state.</li> <li><strong>P1 Phase Gate</strong>: required to close the current phase or unblock the next phase responsibly.</li> <li><strong>P2 Next Slice</strong>: next implementation slice after current phase gates are adequately planned or closed.</li> <li><strong>P3 Research Expansion</strong>: useful experiment or feature, but not needed for current gate.</li> <li><strong>P4 Polish</strong>: quality-of-life, dashboard polish, formatting, cleanup, or presentation work.</li> </ul> <h2 id="ranking-factors">Ranking Factors</h2> <p>Rank higher when a task:</p> <ul> <li>Prevents accidental loss or bad Git history.</li> <li>Produces evidence for the current phase exit checklist.</li> <li>Removes ambiguity for multiple later steps.</li> <li>Is required before physical hardware time is spent.</li> <li>Is cheap to verify and reduces future confusion.</li> <li>Matches the current phase better than jumping ahead.</li> </ul> <p>Rank lower when a task:</p> <ul> <li>Depends on unavailable hardware or supervisor input.</li> <li>Is a later-phase feature.</li> <li>Adds polish before a runnable vertical slice exists.</li> <li>Produces code without a clear run-bundle or test artifact.</li> </ul> <h2 id="ready-shelf-rule">Ready/Shelf Rule</h2> <p>A partially built or proposed task is <strong>READY</strong> only when it has:</p> <ul> <li>one authority document or stream-log pointer,</li> <li>bounded files/modules or a bounded artifact target,</li> <li>explicit acceptance evidence or a verification command,</li> <li>no hidden hardware/user/token-budget dependency, and</li> <li>a named lane (<code>[AGENT]</code>, <code>[QUIET-MAC]</code>, or <code>[ED-EXTERNAL]</code>).</li> </ul> <p>If any of those are missing, keep the item as a shelved concept or planning note instead of letting it compete with executable queue work. Half-finished work should be resumed only through its authority pointer and stop-card/checkpoint state, not by inference from prose summaries.</p> <h2 id="machine-state-lanes-adopted-c-007-2026-07-07">Machine-State Lanes (adopted C-007, 2026-07-07)</h2> <p>Every task carries a lane; a session picks the top task COMPATIBLE with its machine state, not the top task absolutely:</p> <ul> <li><strong>[QUIET-MAC]</strong> — measurement campaigns only: no agent fleet, no Codex load, idle gate will flag contamination.</li> <li><strong>[AGENT]</strong> — code, docs, feasibility spikes; safe during agent-heavy sessions.</li> <li><strong>[ED-EXTERNAL]</strong> — needs the user: advisor, calendar, device access, purchases, destinations.</li> </ul> <h2 id="historical-queue-snapshot-superseded-2026-07-15">Historical Queue Snapshot (superseded 2026-07-15)</h2> <p>The former hand-authored live table was removed because it duplicated kernel tasks. Dated completion and disposition history remains below; the generated Current Queue region is the sole live work-selection view.</p> <h2 id="completed-queue-items">Completed Queue Items</h2> <div class="table-scroll"><table> <thead> <tr> <th>ID</th> <th>Priority</th> <th>Completed</th> <th>Task</th> <th>Evidence</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody><tr> <td>CODEX-BRIDGE-PET</td> <td>P4 Polish</td> <td>2026-07-18</td> <td>Make the native Codex pet reflect Claude Code background Sol work without changing adaptive effort routing</td> <td>No phase exit-checklist row exists for this personal bridge UI integration; de665ea"><span class="source-file">TASK_QUEUE.md</span><span class="source-commit">commit de665ea</span></span></div> <!-- rendered: marked@18.0.6 --> <h1>JouleWise Task Queue</h1> <p>This is the live queue for JouleWise work. When the user gives a new task, first triage it here instead of assuming it should happen immediately.</p> <h2 id="intake-rule-for-new-tasks">Intake Rule For New Tasks</h2> <p>For every new user task:</p> <ol> <li>Read <code>RUN_STATE.md</code>.</li> <li>Read this file.</li> <li>Check <code>git status --short --branch</code>.</li> <li>Review the last 2-3 commits with <code>git log --oneline --decorate -3</code>.</li> <li>Check relevant handoffs in <code>docs/run_reports/</code>.</li> <li>If <code>RUN_STATE.md</code> contains an ACTIVE <code>ACTIVE_STOP_CARD</code>, that card outranks this queue. Execute or preserve the card&#39;s resume/cleanup instructions before considering any lower-ranked work.</li> <li>Decide whether the task is:<ul> <li>urgent workspace hygiene,</li> <li>Phase 1 evidence work,</li> <li>Phase 2 implementation prep,</li> <li>later-phase research work,</li> <li>documentation/reporting,</li> <li>or unrelated/new scope.</li> </ul> </li> <li>Place or update the task in the queue with priority, rationale, evidence, and blockers.</li> <li>If executing it now, say why it outranks the current top task.</li> <li>Closure rule (D-023): a row may move to Completed only after the corresponding phase exit-checklist matrix row already shows the same status with dated evidence, and the Completed row&#39;s evidence cell must cite that matrix row (file + item id). If no matrix row exists for the work, say so explicitly in the evidence cell.</li> </ol> <h2 id="priority-scale">Priority Scale</h2> <ul> <li><strong>P0 Safety</strong>: prevents accidental data loss, bad commits, broken handoffs, or corrupted repo state.</li> <li><strong>P1 Phase Gate</strong>: required to close the current phase or unblock the next phase responsibly.</li> <li><strong>P2 Next Slice</strong>: next implementation slice after current phase gates are adequately planned or closed.</li> <li><strong>P3 Research Expansion</strong>: useful experiment or feature, but not needed for current gate.</li> <li><strong>P4 Polish</strong>: quality-of-life, dashboard polish, formatting, cleanup, or presentation work.</li> </ul> <h2 id="ranking-factors">Ranking Factors</h2> <p>Rank higher when a task:</p> <ul> <li>Prevents accidental loss or bad Git history.</li> <li>Produces evidence for the current phase exit checklist.</li> <li>Removes ambiguity for multiple later steps.</li> <li>Is required before physical hardware time is spent.</li> <li>Is cheap to verify and reduces future confusion.</li> <li>Matches the current phase better than jumping ahead.</li> </ul> <p>Rank lower when a task:</p> <ul> <li>Depends on unavailable hardware or supervisor input.</li> <li>Is a later-phase feature.</li> <li>Adds polish before a runnable vertical slice exists.</li> <li>Produces code without a clear run-bundle or test artifact.</li> </ul> <h2 id="ready-shelf-rule">Ready/Shelf Rule</h2> <p>A partially built or proposed task is <strong>READY</strong> only when it has:</p> <ul> <li>one authority document or stream-log pointer,</li> <li>bounded files/modules or a bounded artifact target,</li> <li>explicit acceptance evidence or a verification command,</li> <li>no hidden hardware/user/token-budget dependency, and</li> <li>a named lane (<code>[AGENT]</code>, <code>[QUIET-MAC]</code>, or <code>[ED-EXTERNAL]</code>).</li> </ul> <p>If any of those are missing, keep the item as a shelved concept or planning note instead of letting it compete with executable queue work. Half-finished work should be resumed only through its authority pointer and stop-card/checkpoint state, not by inference from prose summaries.</p> <h2 id="machine-state-lanes-adopted-c-007-2026-07-07">Machine-State Lanes (adopted C-007, 2026-07-07)</h2> <p>Every task carries a lane; a session picks the top task COMPATIBLE with its machine state, not the top task absolutely:</p> <ul> <li><strong>[QUIET-MAC]</strong> — measurement campaigns only: no agent fleet, no Codex load, idle gate will flag contamination.</li> <li><strong>[AGENT]</strong> — code, docs, feasibility spikes; safe during agent-heavy sessions.</li> <li><strong>[ED-EXTERNAL]</strong> — needs the user: advisor, calendar, device access, purchases, destinations.</li> </ul> <h2 id="historical-queue-snapshot-superseded-2026-07-15">Historical Queue Snapshot (superseded 2026-07-15)</h2> <p>The former hand-authored live table was removed because it duplicated kernel tasks. Dated completion and disposition history remains below; the generated Current Queue region is the sole live work-selection view.</p> <h2 id="completed-queue-items">Completed Queue Items</h2> <div class="table-scroll"><table> <thead> <tr> <th>ID</th> <th>Priority</th> <th>Completed</th> <th>Task</th> <th>Evidence</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody><tr> <td>CODEX-BRIDGE-PET</td> <td>P4 Polish</td> <td>2026-07-18</td> <td>Make the native Codex pet reflect Claude Code background Sol work without changing adaptive effort routing</td> <td>No phase exit-checklist row exists for this personal bridge UI integration; de665ea"><span class="source-file">TASK_QUEUE.md</span><span class="source-commit">commit de665ea</span></span></div> <!-- rendered: marked@18.0.6 --> <h1>JouleWise Task Queue</h1> <p>This is the live queue for JouleWise work. When the user gives a new task, first triage it here instead of assuming it should happen immediately.</p> <h2 id="intake-rule-for-new-tasks">Intake Rule For New Tasks</h2> <p>For every new user task:</p> <ol> <li>Read <code>RUN_STATE.md</code>.</li> <li>Read this file.</li> <li>Check <code>git status --short --branch</code>.</li> <li>Review the last 2-3 commits with <code>git log --oneline --decorate -3</code>.</li> <li>Check relevant handoffs in <code>docs/run_reports/</code>.</li> <li>If <code>RUN_STATE.md</code> contains an ACTIVE <code>ACTIVE_STOP_CARD</code>, that card outranks this queue. Execute or preserve the card&#39;s resume/cleanup instructions before considering any lower-ranked work.</li> <li>Decide whether the task is:<ul> <li>urgent workspace hygiene,</li> <li>Phase 1 evidence work,</li> <li>Phase 2 implementation prep,</li> <li>later-phase research work,</li> <li>documentation/reporting,</li> <li>or unrelated/new scope.</li> </ul> </li> <li>Place or update the task in the queue with priority, rationale, evidence, and blockers.</li> <li>If executing it now, say why it outranks the current top task.</li> <li>Closure rule (D-023): a row may move to Completed only after the corresponding phase exit-checklist matrix row already shows the same status with dated evidence, and the Completed row&#39;s evidence cell must cite that matrix row (file + item id). If no matrix row exists for the work, say so explicitly in the evidence cell.</li> </ol> <h2 id="priority-scale">Priority Scale</h2> <ul> <li><strong>P0 Safety</strong>: prevents accidental data loss, bad commits, broken handoffs, or corrupted repo state.</li> <li><strong>P1 Phase Gate</strong>: required to close the current phase or unblock the next phase responsibly.</li> <li><strong>P2 Next Slice</strong>: next implementation slice after current phase gates are adequately planned or closed.</li> <li><strong>P3 Research Expansion</strong>: useful experiment or feature, but not needed for current gate.</li> <li><strong>P4 Polish</strong>: quality-of-life, dashboard polish, formatting, cleanup, or presentation work.</li> </ul> <h2 id="ranking-factors">Ranking Factors</h2> <p>Rank higher when a task:</p> <ul> <li>Prevents accidental loss or bad Git history.</li> <li>Produces evidence for the current phase exit checklist.</li> <li>Removes ambiguity for multiple later steps.</li> <li>Is required before physical hardware time is spent.</li> <li>Is cheap to verify and reduces future confusion.</li> <li>Matches the current phase better than jumping ahead.</li> </ul> <p>Rank lower when a task:</p> <ul> <li>Depends on unavailable hardware or supervisor input.</li> <li>Is a later-phase feature.</li> <li>Adds polish before a runnable vertical slice exists.</li> <li>Produces code without a clear run-bundle or test artifact.</li> </ul> <h2 id="ready-shelf-rule">Ready/Shelf Rule</h2> <p>A partially built or proposed task is <strong>READY</strong> only when it has:</p> <ul> <li>one authority document or stream-log pointer,</li> <li>bounded files/modules or a bounded artifact target,</li> <li>explicit acceptance evidence or a verification command,</li> <li>no hidden hardware/user/token-budget dependency, and</li> <li>a named lane (<code>[AGENT]</code>, <code>[QUIET-MAC]</code>, or <code>[ED-EXTERNAL]</code>).</li> </ul> <p>If any of those are missing, keep the item as a shelved concept or planning note instead of letting it compete with executable queue work. Half-finished work should be resumed only through its authority pointer and stop-card/checkpoint state, not by inference from prose summaries.</p> <h2 id="machine-state-lanes-adopted-c-007-2026-07-07">Machine-State Lanes (adopted C-007, 2026-07-07)</h2> <p>Every task carries a lane; a session picks the top task COMPATIBLE with its machine state, not the top task absolutely:</p> <ul> <li><strong>[QUIET-MAC]</strong> — measurement campaigns only: no agent fleet, no Codex load, idle gate will flag contamination.</li> <li><strong>[AGENT]</strong> — code, docs, feasibility spikes; safe during agent-heavy sessions.</li> <li><strong>[ED-EXTERNAL]</strong> — needs the user: advisor, calendar, device access, purchases, destinations.</li> </ul> <h2 id="historical-queue-snapshot-superseded-2026-07-15">Historical Queue Snapshot (superseded 2026-07-15)</h2> <p>The former hand-authored live table was removed because it duplicated kernel tasks. Dated completion and disposition history remains below; the generated Current Queue region is the sole live work-selection view.</p> <h2 id="completed-queue-items">Completed Queue Items</h2> <div class="table-scroll"><table> <thead> <tr> <th>ID</th> <th>Priority</th> <th>Completed</th> <th>Task</th> <th>Evidence</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody><tr> <td>CODEX-BRIDGE-PET</td> <td>P4 Polish</td> <td>2026-07-18</td> <td>Make the native Codex pet reflect Claude Code background Sol work without changing adaptive effort routing</td> <td>No phase exit-checklist row exists for this personal bridge UI integration; de665ea"><span class="source-file">TASK_QUEUE.md</span><span class="source-commit">commit de665ea</span></span></div> <!-- rendered: marked@18.0.6 --> <h1>JouleWise Task Queue</h1> <p>This is the live queue for JouleWise work. When the user gives a new task, first triage it here instead of assuming it should happen immediately.</p> <h2 id="intake-rule-for-new-tasks">Intake Rule For New Tasks</h2> <p>For every new user task:</p> <ol> <li>Read <code>RUN_STATE.md</code>.</li> <li>Read this file.</li> <li>Check <code>git status --short --branch</code>.</li> <li>Review the last 2-3 commits with <code>git log --oneline --decorate -3</code>.</li> <li>Check relevant handoffs in <code>docs/run_reports/</code>.</li> <li>If <code>RUN_STATE.md</code> contains an ACTIVE <code>ACTIVE_STOP_CARD</code>, that card outranks this queue. Execute or preserve the card&#39;s resume/cleanup instructions before considering any lower-ranked work.</li> <li>Decide whether the task is:<ul> <li>urgent workspace hygiene,</li> <li>Phase 1 evidence work,</li> <li>Phase 2 implementation prep,</li> <li>later-phase research work,</li> <li>documentation/reporting,</li> <li>or unrelated/new scope.</li> </ul> </li> <li>Place or update the task in the queue with priority, rationale, evidence, and blockers.</li> <li>If executing it now, say why it outranks the current top task.</li> <li>Closure rule (D-023): a row may move to Completed only after the corresponding phase exit-checklist matrix row already shows the same status with dated evidence, and the Completed row&#39;s evidence cell must cite that matrix row (file + item id). If no matrix row exists for the work, say so explicitly in the evidence cell.</li> </ol> <h2 id="priority-scale">Priority Scale</h2> <ul> <li><strong>P0 Safety</strong>: prevents accidental data loss, bad commits, broken handoffs, or corrupted repo state.</li> <li><strong>P1 Phase Gate</strong>: required to close the current phase or unblock the next phase responsibly.</li> <li><strong>P2 Next Slice</strong>: next implementation slice after current phase gates are adequately planned or closed.</li> <li><strong>P3 Research Expansion</strong>: useful experiment or feature, but not needed for current gate.</li> <li><strong>P4 Polish</strong>: quality-of-life, dashboard polish, formatting, cleanup, or presentation work.</li> </ul> <h2 id="ranking-factors">Ranking Factors</h2> <p>Rank higher when a task:</p> <ul> <li>Prevents accidental loss or bad Git history.</li> <li>Produces evidence for the current phase exit checklist.</li> <li>Removes ambiguity for multiple later steps.</li> <li>Is required before physical hardware time is spent.</li> <li>Is cheap to verify and reduces future confusion.</li> <li>Matches the current phase better than jumping ahead.</li> </ul> <p>Rank lower when a task:</p> <ul> <li>Depends on unavailable hardware or supervisor input.</li> <li>Is a later-phase feature.</li> <li>Adds polish before a runnable vertical slice exists.</li> <li>Produces code without a clear run-bundle or test artifact.</li> </ul> <h2 id="ready-shelf-rule">Ready/Shelf Rule</h2> <p>A partially built or proposed task is <strong>READY</strong> only when it has:</p> <ul> <li>one authority document or stream-log pointer,</li> <li>bounded files/modules or a bounded artifact target,</li> <li>explicit acceptance evidence or a verification command,</li> <li>no hidden hardware/user/token-budget dependency, and</li> <li>a named lane (<code>[AGENT]</code>, <code>[QUIET-MAC]</code>, or <code>[ED-EXTERNAL]</code>).</li> </ul> <p>If any of those are missing, keep the item as a shelved concept or planning note instead of letting it compete with executable queue work. Half-finished work should be resumed only through its authority pointer and stop-card/checkpoint state, not by inference from prose summaries.</p> <h2 id="machine-state-lanes-adopted-c-007-2026-07-07">Machine-State Lanes (adopted C-007, 2026-07-07)</h2> <p>Every task carries a lane; a session picks the top task COMPATIBLE with its machine state, not the top task absolutely:</p> <ul> <li><strong>[QUIET-MAC]</strong> — measurement campaigns only: no agent fleet, no Codex load, idle gate will flag contamination.</li> <li><strong>[AGENT]</strong> — code, docs, feasibility spikes; safe during agent-heavy sessions.</li> <li><strong>[ED-EXTERNAL]</strong> — needs the user: advisor, calendar, device access, purchases, destinations.</li> </ul> <h2 id="historical-queue-snapshot-superseded-2026-07-15">Historical Queue Snapshot (superseded 2026-07-15)</h2> <p>The former hand-authored live table was removed because it duplicated kernel tasks. Dated completion and disposition history remains below; the generated Current Queue region is the sole live work-selection view.</p> <h2 id="completed-queue-items">Completed Queue Items</h2> <div class="table-scroll"><table> <thead> <tr> <th>ID</th> <th>Priority</th> <th>Completed</th> <th>Task</th> <th>Evidence</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody><tr> <td>CODEX-BRIDGE-PET</td> <td>P4 Polish</td> <td>2026-07-18</td> <td>Make the native Codex pet reflect Claude Code background Sol work without changing adaptive effort routing</td> <td>No phase exit-checklist row exists for this personal bridge UI integration; <!-- rendered: marked@18.0.6 --> <h1>JouleWise Task Queue</h1> <p>This is the live queue for JouleWise work. When the user gives a new task, first triage it here instead of assuming it should happen immediately.</p> <h2 id="intake-rule-for-new-tasks">Intake Rule For New Tasks</h2> <p>For every new user task:</p> <ol> <li>Read <code>RUN_STATE.md</code>.</li> <li>Read this file.</li> <li>Check <code>git status --short --branch</code>.</li> <li>Review the last 2-3 commits with <code>git log --oneline --decorate -3</code>.</li> <li>Check relevant handoffs in <code>docs/run_reports/</code>.</li> <li>If <code>RUN_STATE.md</code> contains an ACTIVE <code>ACTIVE_STOP_CARD</code>, that card outranks this queue. Execute or preserve the card&#39;s resume/cleanup instructions before considering any lower-ranked work.</li> <li>Decide whether the task is:<ul> <li>urgent workspace hygiene,</li> <li>Phase 1 evidence work,</li> <li>Phase 2 implementation prep,</li> <li>later-phase research work,</li> <li>documentation/reporting,</li> <li>or unrelated/new scope.</li> </ul> </li> <li>Place or update the task in the queue with priority, rationale, evidence, and blockers.</li> <li>If executing it now, say why it outranks the current top task.</li> <li>Closure rule (D-023): a row may move to Completed only after the corresponding phase exit-checklist matrix row already shows the same status with dated evidence, and the Completed row&#39;s evidence cell must cite that matrix row (file + item id). If no matrix row exists for the work, say so explicitly in the evidence cell.</li> </ol> <h2 id="priority-scale">Priority Scale</h2> <ul> <li><strong>P0 Safety</strong>: prevents accidental data loss, bad commits, broken handoffs, or corrupted repo state.</li> <li><strong>P1 Phase Gate</strong>: required to close the current phase or unblock the next phase responsibly.</li> <li><strong>P2 Next Slice</strong>: next implementation slice after current phase gates are adequately planned or closed.</li> <li><strong>P3 Research Expansion</strong>: useful experiment or feature, but not needed for current gate.</li> <li><strong>P4 Polish</strong>: quality-of-life, dashboard polish, formatting, cleanup, or presentation work.</li> </ul> <h2 id="ranking-factors">Ranking Factors</h2> <p>Rank higher when a task:</p> <ul> <li>Prevents accidental loss or bad Git history.</li> <li>Produces evidence for the current phase exit checklist.</li> <li>Removes ambiguity for multiple later steps.</li> <li>Is required before physical hardware time is spent.</li> <li>Is cheap to verify and reduces future confusion.</li> <li>Matches the current phase better than jumping ahead.</li> </ul> <p>Rank lower when a task:</p> <ul> <li>Depends on unavailable hardware or supervisor input.</li> <li>Is a later-phase feature.</li> <li>Adds polish before a runnable vertical slice exists.</li> <li>Produces code without a clear run-bundle or test artifact.</li> </ul> <h2 id="ready-shelf-rule">Ready/Shelf Rule</h2> <p>A partially built or proposed task is <strong>READY</strong> only when it has:</p> <ul> <li>one authority document or stream-log pointer,</li> <li>bounded files/modules or a bounded artifact target,</li> <li>explicit acceptance evidence or a verification command,</li> <li>no hidden hardware/user/token-budget dependency, and</li> <li>a named lane (<code>[AGENT]</code>, <code>[QUIET-MAC]</code>, or <code>[ED-EXTERNAL]</code>).</li> </ul> <p>If any of those are missing, keep the item as a shelved concept or planning note instead of letting it compete with executable queue work. Half-finished work should be resumed only through its authority pointer and stop-card/checkpoint state, not by inference from prose summaries.</p> <h2 id="machine-state-lanes-adopted-c-007-2026-07-07">Machine-State Lanes (adopted C-007, 2026-07-07)</h2> <p>Every task carries a lane; a session picks the top task COMPATIBLE with its machine state, not the top task absolutely:</p> <ul> <li><strong>[QUIET-MAC]</strong> — measurement campaigns only: no agent fleet, no Codex load, idle gate will flag contamination.</li> <li><strong>[AGENT]</strong> — code, docs, feasibility spikes; safe during agent-heavy sessions.</li> <li><strong>[ED-EXTERNAL]</strong> — needs the user: advisor, calendar, device access, purchases, destinations.</li> </ul> <h2 id="historical-queue-snapshot-superseded-2026-07-15">Historical Queue Snapshot (superseded 2026-07-15)</h2> <p>The former hand-authored live table was removed because it duplicated kernel tasks. Dated completion and disposition history remains below; the generated Current Queue region is the sole live work-selection view.</p> <h2 id="completed-queue-items">Completed Queue Items</h2> <div class="table-scroll"><table> <thead> <tr> <th>ID</th> <th>Priority</th> <th>Completed</th> <th>Task</th> <th>Evidence</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody><tr> <td>CODEX-BRIDGE-PET</td> <td>P4 Polish</td> <td>2026-07-18</td> <td>Make the native Codex pet reflect Claude Code background Sol work without changing adaptive effort routing</td> <td>No phase exit-checklist row exists for this personal bridge UI integration; Evidence: Block-timescale fiducial stationarity registered as a NAMED transfer assumption with its evidence; Estimator pre-registered before it touches claim-bearing data; The identical estimator applied to BOTH the calibration blocks and the consuming science contrast (a floor calibrated with cancellation the consumer does not get would understate false effects); Quantified gain on a5/a10 blocks versus the worst-case-sum default. Authority: <a href="docs/decision_log.md">2026-07-25 attribution-limit adjudication (Fable ruling + Sol replay; plan in session scratchpad)</a>. Quantified same day on a5 decode ABBA (10 complete blocks): implemented worst-case-sum half-width gives a 6.46 J comparative floor; a common-mode proxy gives 2.13 J, a 3x improvement — material, but still above that cell&#x27;s 0.60 J point floor, so it does not by itself restore extraction under the current gate. Value is in tightening the labelled floor, not in avoiding the label. Fiducial share of the composed bound measured at 80-87%.</p></details> <span class="source-chip" title="TASK_QUEUE.md · commit de665ea"><span class="source-file">TASK_QUEUE.md</span><span class="source-commit">commit de665ea</span></span> </div> </article><article class="lane-card" data-lane="AGENT"> <div class="priority-band p2"></div> <div class="lane-main"> <div class="lane-head"><span class="lane-rank mono">#A48</span><span class="mono task-code">PHASE-SHARE-ESTIMAND-01</span><span class="status-chip">READY</span><span class="lane-chip lane-agent">AGENT</span></div> <p class="status-note">READY</p> <h2>Investigate the anti-correlated prefill/decode boundary error: energy a shift removes from one phase it adds to the other, so the phase-share estimand has ONE boundary nuisance parameter whose joint envelope is a curve, not a box.</h2> <details><summary>Acceptance</summary><p>Treating each phase&#x27;s anchor envelope as an independent box double-spends the shared interior boundary and inflates uncertainty on exactly the split/share quantity the Splitwise replication needs. docs/paper/draft-v1.md-1-# JouleWise: Attribution-Limited Detection Floors for Phase-Resolved LLM Inference Energy on Apple Silicon
docs/paper/draft-v1.md-2-
docs/paper/draft-v1.md-3-*Draft: demonstration values, instrument-characterization results, and archive locators are pending; bracketed markers show where they will land.*
docs/paper/draft-v1.md-4-
docs/paper/draft-v1.md-5-## Abstract
docs/paper/draft-v1.md-6-
docs/paper/draft-v1.md:7:Published energy figures for large language model (LLM) inference rarely state the smallest difference their measurement method can trust. This omission matters on consumer hardware, where Apple's *powermetrics* utility estimates processor power without a laboratory meter and where small timing errors can move energy across the boundary between prompt processing and token generation. JouleWise treats the software counter as a scientific instrument. It marks phase boundaries in the runtime, calibrates how far sampled power edges can shift, and combines measured repeatability, worst-case boundary attribution, and drift into a *detection floor*: the smallest difference the method can trust under the stated conditions. Missing, stale, or inconsistent evidence produces a refusal rather than an optimistic result. The main physical finding is that a boundary-timing uncertainty of roughly 30 ms during a power swing of roughly 33 W can move about one joule into the wrong phase; because this is an attribution error rather than random scatter, repetition cannot remove it. Floor clearance and interval-supported direction are therefore enforced as separate gates. When attribution dominance is the sole publication issue, the floor is published with an explicit label naming that limitation. The method is scoped to one named Apple-silicon machine, software stack, and measurement boundary. The demonstration applies the discipline to phase-resolved measurements of two model sizes and will report whether each registered contrast is resolvable or must be refused.
docs/paper/draft-v1.md-8-
docs/paper/draft-v1.md-9-## 1. Introduction
docs/paper/draft-v1.md-10-
docs/paper/draft-v1.md-11-Energy numbers for large language model (LLM) inference now appear in leaderboards, systems papers, product comparisons, and policy debates. Published estimates for apparently similar queries can differ by an order of magnitude, yet the numbers are rarely accompanied by an error bar that says how small a difference the measurement method can actually distinguish. This omission is especially consequential on consumer hardware. Apple's *powermetrics* utility makes processor power estimates available without a laboratory meter and is therefore attractive for repeated experiments, but, to our knowledge, it has not been validated in published work as an instrument for separating the energy of LLM inference phases. Apple describes its outputs as estimates; treating them as exact readings can turn timing uncertainty at a phase boundary into a spurious energy difference.
docs/paper/draft-v1.md-12-
docs/paper/draft-v1.md-13-The core difficulty is physical as much as statistical. Energy is the integral of power over time. An experiment may repeat consistently and still assign energy to the wrong phase if a power sample near the boundary between prompt processing and token generation is placed on the wrong side. Averaging more repetitions reduces random scatter but does not remove that attribution error. Slow changes in thermal or background state can add a second false difference over a long collection session.
--
docs/paper/draft-v1.md-113-where \(F_{\mathrm{cell}}\) is also an energy magnitude in joules. The components are not summed. Cross-window components keep their own calibration basis and allowance; an allowance is never added again at the cell or reporting level. Operative floor values and their full decomposition for each demonstration stack are withheld until corrected artifacts are issued: **[RESULT PENDING CORRECTED ARTIFACTS]**.
docs/paper/draft-v1.md-114-
docs/paper/draft-v1.md-115-### Publication label and the two claim gates
docs/paper/draft-v1.md-116-
docs/paper/draft-v1.md-117-When timing attribution dominates, a floor may be published with an explicit attribution-limited label only if that dominance is the sole otherwise-refusing condition and an exact corner-widened floor exists. The published result identifies the dominant source as energy uncertainty caused by shifting the phase edges within the calibrated clock-anchor bound. It publishes the corner-widened value rather than the smaller point diagnostic and retains the point-only repeatability value as a diagnostic that cannot support a claim. The label never rescues any other refusal: missing, stale, contaminated, or inconsistent evidence remains terminal.
docs/paper/draft-v1.md-118-
docs/paper/draft-v1.md:119:A claim then faces two separate gates, enforced separately. First, the magnitude of its point estimate must exceed \(F_{\mathrm{cell}}\), the cell floor. Second, both endpoints of its fully composed decision interval must support the pre-registered direction. Let \(B_{\mathrm{claim}}\) be the claim-side measurement-uncertainty magnitude in joules carried by that interval. The project also discloses
docs/paper/draft-v1.md-120-
docs/paper/draft-v1.md-121-\[
docs/paper/draft-v1.md-122-\text{practical joint-clearance size}=F_{\mathrm{cell}}+B_{\mathrm{claim}}.
docs/paper/draft-v1.md-123-\]
docs/paper/draft-v1.md-124-
docs/paper/draft-v1.md-125-For the measured phase-contrast regime, this practical sizing quantity is several joules. It explains how large an effect will generally need to be to clear both gates together and ensures that neither physical uncertainty term is hidden as an apparent double count. It is not a single summed acceptance threshold, and the decision interval is not compared with the sum. Effects that fail the floor gate are reported as *not resolvable*, not as zero, equal, or evidence of no difference. Effects that pass the floor gate but whose interval does not support direction remain unresolved and receive no directional claim.
--
docs/paper/draft-v1.md-129-*Fail-closed* means that missing, inconsistent, stale, or contaminated evidence produces a refusal rather than an optimistic default. The collection unit is the measurement window defined in Section 3. Work that does not fit within two to four hours with at least a 20% failure margin is split prospectively into another independently calibrated window.
docs/paper/draft-v1.md-130-
docs/paper/draft-v1.md-131-### Pre-registration and admission
docs/paper/draft-v1.md-132-
docs/paper/draft-v1.md-133-Before quiet time, the operator freezes the run identifiers, membership, stage order, comparison definitions, calibration retry count, acceptance thresholds, extraction specification, code revision, and an initially empty waiver list. Every configuration is validated and dry-run against a fresh collection directory. These choices are made before outcomes are visible. Pre-registration here is executable: the launcher and final verifier check the frozen values rather than relying on a narrative promise.
docs/paper/draft-v1.md-134-
docs/paper/draft-v1.md:135:Prospective sizing is part of that freeze. Before collection, the planned effect, workload, and number of independent bundles or ABBA blocks are compared with the cell floor and the claim-side interval width. If the design has too little expected clearance, the operator must prospectively increase independent evidence, change the workload, or narrow the claim; the choice cannot be made after seeing claim data. A workload change is not merely a sensitivity adjustment. For example, lengthening the prompt changes the population of requests being estimated and therefore changes the estimand itself.
docs/paper/draft-v1.md-136-
docs/paper/draft-v1.md-137-Each stage then passes admission gates immediately before measurement. The approved power supply and power policy must be unchanged; displays must be asleep; the screensaver and low-power mode must be off; thermal pressure must be nominal; and central- and graphics-processor activity must meet the quiet-state criteria. Known background work is allowed to finish before the window, followed by a settling interval, rather than being ignored during analysis. Runtime and telemetry identities, clock anchoring, sample cadence, calibration freshness, and post-run environment observations are also checked. No environment override can produce a claim-bearing member.
docs/paper/draft-v1.md-138-
docs/paper/draft-v1.md-139-### Counterbalanced order
docs/paper/draft-v1.md-140-
docs/paper/draft-v1.md-141-Comparisons use the ABBA blocks defined in Section 4. Conditions A and B are measured in the order A, B, B, A, with ordinary cooldown between members. Averaging the two outer A observations and the two inner B observations cancels a linear time trend within the block to first order. For null-floor calibration, A and B are aliases of the same configuration and payload, so any nonzero block difference is a false comparative effect. For scientific contrasts, the A and B definitions are frozen in advance, and the contrast is computed within each block before blocks are aggregated. ABBA reduces common drift; it does not replace the measured whole-window drift allowance.
--

docs/paper/draft-v1.md-242-Split, or disaggregated, inference places prompt processing and token generation on different devices and transfers intermediate state between them. Revisiting Disaggregated Large Language Model Serving reports essentially unconditionally higher energy for disaggregation on its evaluated two-graphics-processor node, while its performance benefits depend on load, baseline, and transfer conditions [13]. Its energy boundary combines several software telemetry sources into whole-run energy per token. DualScale studies phase placement and per-phase power control but reports graphics-processor-only energy from homogeneous server hardware [14]. Prima.cpp includes whole-run energy and communication accounting but not a per-stage energy split [15], while SplitZip characterizes lossless transfer compression without making an energy claim [16].
docs/paper/draft-v1.md-243-
docs/paper/draft-v1.md-244-JouleWise does not claim a new split scheduler in this paper. Split inference is instead a demanding future demonstration of the instrument because it introduces two physical boundaries, a transfer interval, and clock alignment across devices. A valid comparison would have to measure both ends, name each boundary, and pass a pre-registered floor or calibrated bridge. Whether splitting saves energy remains an empirical outcome; the reusable contribution is a method that can issue, qualify, or refuse the result.
docs/paper/draft-v1.md-245-
docs/paper/draft-v1.md-246-## 10. Limitations
docs/paper/draft-v1.md-247-
docs/paper/draft-v1.md:248:**Attribution-limited resolution.** The dominant uncertainty on the studied implementation is boundary placement, not scatter. Roughly one joule per phase member can be misassigned when calibrated timing uncertainty of tens of milliseconds meets a power swing of tens of watts, and repetitions do not reduce it. When attribution dominance is the sole otherwise-refusing condition and an exact corner-widened floor exists, the result may be published with an explicit attribution-limited label; that label never rescues any other refusal. The floor plus claim-side bound remains a practical several-joule sizing disclosure, not one summed acceptance threshold. A historical non-claim diagnostic of the short-prompt model-size contrast had a point estimate marginally above that practical bar, but its composed interval overlapped the bar. That diagnostic motivated the prospective floors-only prompt-processing default in Section 7; it was not a fresh measurement or an issued refusal. The resulting limitation concerns what this implementation, on the named stack and boundary, can support.
docs/paper/draft-v1.md-249-
docs/paper/draft-v1.md-250-**One unit, one stack, one boundary.** Every result is scoped to one physical machine, operating-system build, runtime and library stack, model artifact, quantization, tokenizer, sampling and output policy, telemetry backend, and measurement boundary. Nothing here ranks hardware classes or vendors, and the whole-system-on-chip boundary of *powermetrics* is not comparable to a graphics-board or wall boundary without a calibrated bridge.
docs/paper/draft-v1.md-251-
docs/paper/draft-v1.md-252-**No external meter.** The calibration validates timing attribution—whether samples near a commanded edge land inside or outside a phase integral. It does not validate the counter's absolute gain or whole-system scale; absolute joule values remain internal to the named software boundary. A wall-power instrument could test totals but would still not adjudicate the division of a total between phases, which is the question the pulse-train experiment answers.
docs/paper/draft-v1.md-253-
docs/paper/draft-v1.md-254-**Transfer assumptions.** The calibration pulses are graphics-processor matrix multiplications under light central-processor load; transferring their timing bound to sustained mixed-load inference is an explicit assumption, constrained by the in-window bracket and the planned empirical floor probes but not eliminated. The drift allowance is measured per window with no duration-scaling law because the evidence does not identify one; longer windows than those characterized would need fresh drift evidence.
--

TASK_QUEUE.md:376:| A47 | FLOOR-COMMONMODE-01 | P2 Next Slice | READY [AGENT] | Pre-register and evaluate a common-mode anchor estimator for ABBA blocks: sweep one shared fiducial shift across all four members, re-integrate measured curves, and add only genuinely per-bundle components adversarially. | The fiducial term is ~80% of the composed anchor bound (24.9 of ~31.1 ms, verified) and is literally the same artifact for all four members of a block; treating it as four independent adversarial draws is itself an unphysical modelling choice. Evidence: Block-timescale fiducial stationarity registered as a NAMED transfer assumption with its evidence; Estimator pre-registered before it touches claim-bearing data; The identical estimator applied to BOTH the calibration blocks and the consuming science contrast (a floor calibrated with cancellation the consumer does not get would understate false effects); Quantified gain on a5/a10 blocks versus the worst-case-sum default. Authority: [2026-07-25 attribution-limit adjudication (Fable ruling + Sol replay; plan in session scratchpad)](docs/decision_log.md). Acceptance: [FLOOR-COMMONMODE-01 acceptance](docs/process/state_kernel.json). Note: Minted 2026-07-25. Quantified same day on a5 decode ABBA (10 complete blocks): implemented worst-case-sum half-width gives a 6.46 J comparative floor; a common-mode proxy gives 2.13 J, a 3x improvement — material, but still above that cell's 0.60 J point floor, so it does not by itself restore extraction under the current gate. Value is in tightening the labelled floor, not in avoiding the label. Fiducial share of the composed bound measured at 80-87%. |

docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/SYNTHESIS-PRAGMATICS-FIRST.md-11159-Sizing is uncertain. The repo’s non-claim diagnostic is about **0.098 J/decode token** for 1.5B Q4, or roughly **50 J at 512 tokens**. An official MLX benchmark on a different Qwen model and M4 Max reports adjacent generation-throughput differences of roughly 10–17%; at comparable power, that suggests approximately **4–10 J [high-uncertainty estimate]** per adjacent 512-token contrast, with Q5–Q6 the most likely miss. Q4–Q8 should be materially larger. These estimates are extrapolations, not priors to select results; the official data also show that bit width changes quality and performance nonlinearly. [MLX benchmark table](https://github.com/ml-explore/mlx-lm/blob/main/mlx_lm/BENCHMARKS.md)

docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/SYNTHESIS-PRAGMATICS-FIRST.md-11198-
docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/SYNTHESIS-PRAGMATICS-FIRST.md-11199-JouleWise already has the scientific core of this paper: an in-window calibrated `powermetrics` instrument; an attribution-limited finding of roughly 1 J per phase member; LABELLED floors composed from repeatability, worst-case edge placement, and never-zero drift; separate floor-clearance and interval-direction gates; and a fail-closed protocol with pre-registration, admission checks, counterbalancing, hash-bound custody, and published refusals. No claim-bearing numbers currently exist: historical values are diagnostic only. D-117 therefore requires three fresh prospective windows—1.5B decode floor, 7B decode floor, and 1.5B-versus-7B decode contrast—with prefill floors riding the first two. Before those nights, the two-slot live-calibration ledger, D-102 successor path, multi-cell mint, frozen plans, extraction specifications, and synthetic regressions must land. Those three approximately 2.8–3.25-hour windows then mint four phase-floor cells and the model-size contrast, after which the existing draft can be populated.
docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/SYNTHESIS-PRAGMATICS-FIRST.md-11200-
docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/SYNTHESIS-PRAGMATICS-FIRST.md:11201:This paper keeps that spine intact and adds a conditional four-window extension on the owned Mac. The subject is Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct because its 4-bit condition and exact 128-prompt/512-output workload already occur in D-117. From one frozen BF16 source revision, derive affine group-64 Q4/Q5/Q6/Q8 artifacts with identical converter, module allowlist, tokenizer, runtime, and sampling policy. Run the existing 256-item, four-stratum quality screen outside quiet time, using BF16 only as the quality reference. Then collect separate Q5, Q6, and Q8 decode-plus-prefill floor windows; the D-117 Q4 floor supplies the fourth rung. Finally, run one 48-member, 12-block balanced four-arm contrast window. Total funding request: the three D-117 nights plus **four extension nights**, approximately **12–15 additional quiet-machine hours [estimate]**, with no new apparatus.

docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/SYNTHESIS-PRAGMATICS-FIRST.md-13058-### 1. `mvp-icpe-upgrade` — fund, but as the corrected metrology capstone
docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/SYNTHESIS-PRAGMATICS-FIRST.md-13059-
docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/SYNTHESIS-PRAGMATICS-FIRST.md:13060:The submitted “ICPE upgrade” was correctly judged WEAK because its cross-window Q4 prediction is unauthorized and its WT310E arm is neither necessary nor securely available. The surviving paper is nevertheless the highest-certainty and highest-priority portfolio item: the calibrated instrument, attribution limit, floor calculus, refusal protocol, D-117 floors, and prospective decode contrast. Add Window C’s held-out floor-validation ladder, not the proposed multi-night workload matrix. Honest cost is **four planned nights, about 11.2–13.2 quiet hours, 3–6 desk weeks, plus one reserved rerun slot**. Estimated first-pass survival of all four windows is only **60–70%** given the project’s history; completion with one governed reserve is roughly **80–90%**. This is the only item that must proceed regardless of every later ranking.
docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/SYNTHESIS-PRAGMATICS-FIRST.md-13061-
docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/SYNTHESIS-PRAGMATICS-FIRST.md-13062-### 2. `quantization-ladder` — the best second-paper bet
docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/SYNTHESIS-PRAGMATICS-FIRST.md-13063-
docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/SYNTHESIS-PRAGMATICS-FIRST.md:13064:The VIABLE verdict holds only after shrinking to **BF16/Q4/Q8**, deleting Q5/Q6, deleting the unbuilt JouleWise quality gate, and framing the result as precision- and kernel-specific *resolvability*, not quality-neutral efficiency. The D-117 1.5B Q4 floor and exact 128/512 workload carry directly into the paper. BF16 and Q8 still need their own floors, followed by a three-arm contrast: **4+3 nights**, **4–8 incremental desk weeks**, and one reserve slot. A BF16–Q4 result should be loud; Q4–Q8 is the scientifically useful anomaly test and may resolve or refuse. Estimated survival after the capability smoke is **65–75%**. This is lower novelty than a mechanism paper, but far lower operational risk and the best match to the priority rule.
docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/SYNTHESIS-PRAGMATICS-FIRST.md-13065-
docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/SYNTHESIS-PRAGMATICS-FIRST.md-13066-### 3. `moe-routing-energy` — stretch, re-anchored and more expensive
docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/SYNTHESIS-PRAGMATICS-FIRST.md-13067-
docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/SYNTHESIS-PRAGMATICS-FIRST.md:13068:The VIABLE judgment is persuasive, but the 65 GB Qwen3.5-122B VLM/hybrid reasoning checkpoint should not be the claim vehicle. Use the referee’s re-anchor: **Qwen3-30B-A3B versus a dense Qwen3-4B partner**, with native-*k* versus forced-*k* as the causal within-checkpoint leg. This gives the paper both an interpretable dense comparison and a mechanism intervention. It also creates three separately scoped floor cells—native MoE, forced-*k* MoE, and dense—so the honest cost is **4+3–4 nights**, **6–12 desk weeks**, and a reserve, not two nights. Routing-sidecar overhead, output-divergence-induced routing locality, and projected floors can all kill it before collection. Estimated pre-night survival is **35–50%**. This is the right stretch because its ceiling is much higher than quantization’s, not because it is safer.
docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/SYNTHESIS-PRAGMATICS-FIRST.md-13069-
docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/SYNTHESIS-PRAGMATICS-FIRST.md-13070-### 4. `floor-methodology-general` — absorb into the MVP; do not publish separately
docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/SYNTHESIS-PRAGMATICS-FIRST.md-13071-
docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/SYNTHESIS-PRAGMATICS-FIRST.md:13072:The referee was right: this has the portfolio’s best framing—“from repeatability to resolvability”—and an unfundable portability experiment. The NVML/RAPL battery neither transports the phase-attribution finding nor respects existing fences. The surviving content is the MVP’s intellectual packaging plus Window C’s held-out effect ladder. Cost is therefore **the same four MVP nights**, with roughly **1–3 additional desk weeks** for the ladder analysis, refusal taxonomy, and prose. Probability of a useful result is **70–80%** because both correct refusals and correct resolutions support the thesis. Rank four reflects its value to the capstone, not authorization for a second manuscript.
docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/SYNTHESIS-PRAGMATICS-FIRST.md-13073-
docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/SYNTHESIS-PRAGMATICS-FIRST.md-13074-### 5. `long-generation-dynamics` — retain the interior-chunk insight, redesign before any paper
docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/SYNTHESIS-PRAGMATICS-FIRST.md-13075-
docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/SYNTHESIS-PRAGMATICS-FIRST.md:13076:The proposal was WEAK because early-versus-late position is uncounterbalanceable and lacks a legitimate comparative floor. Its important discovery is different: attribution limitation is a **phase-boundary property**, not necessarily a global instrument property. Interior decode-chunk edges may be repeatability-limited near 0.3 J. First make that a desk-only MVP characterization figure. A later paper would need an intervention—bounded versus unbounded cache, or matched-position starting-KV variation—rather than observational token position. Claim-bearing cost is **4+1–2 nights** and **4–8 desk weeks** for chunk reduction, floor semantics, and refusal tests. Estimated survival after the runtime and floor gate is **45–60%**.
docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/SYNTHESIS-PRAGMATICS-FIRST.md-13077-
docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/SYNTHESIS-PRAGMATICS-FIRST.md-13078-### 6. `open-explore-registry` — keep only the prefix-reuse boundary/refusal paper
docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/SYNTHESIS-PRAGMATICS-FIRST.md-13079-
docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/SYNTHESIS-PRAGMATICS-FIRST.md:13080:The tag is WEAK as a three-paper portfolio, but its prefix-reuse idea is the only genuinely new asset-mined direction. The stated “crossover” is arithmetic—if building the cache is the avoided prefill, reuse wins at request two—while the empirical cache load/save overhead is probably below the instrument’s floor. The scientifically honest paper is therefore about what prefix reuse saves, what its SoC boundary misses in off-SoC cache I/O, and which overheads must be refused as unresolvable. Restrict to 2048/4096-token endpoints and mint matching gross/length floors inside **two extension windows**: **4+2 nights**, **3–5 desk weeks**, estimated survival **55–65%**. It is a credible alternate second paper if quantization dies at its desk gate.

docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/SYNTHESIS-PRAGMATICS-FIRST.md-13082-### 7. `kv-context-energy` — fund only a self-floored 1.5B endpoint study
docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/SYNTHESIS-PRAGMATICS-FIRST.md-13083-
docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/SYNTHESIS-PRAGMATICS-FIRST.md:13084:The original four-length, two-model “curve” is a borderline KILL: floor transport is anti-conservative, 7B faces the measured ~14 J comparative floor, and long-prefill thermal carryover is perfectly aligned with the claimed KV effect. A viable residue is one 1.5B long-context endpoint, longer decode to amplify the effect, a same-window long-context null floor, and a separate thermal-matched control. That is **two extension nights**, possibly three if the longer workload breaks the four-hour envelope: **4+2 planned, book 4+3**, with **3–6 desk weeks** and about **35–50%** survival. Do not arm 7B unless the fresh beta floor and local sizing independently support it.

docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/SYNTHESIS-PRAGMATICS-FIRST.md-13087-
docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/SYNTHESIS-PRAGMATICS-FIRST.md:13088:The paper remains WEAK: it needs a gross-request floor class, reopens a closed observability verdict, and existing local evidence shows speculative paths at only 0.36–0.41× baseline throughput. Its upside and alignment with Ed’s original goals still justify one cheap action: run the stock-runtime daytime tok/s pilot before a fork or floor work. Estimated probability that it survives that gate is only **15–25%**. If it unexpectedly passes, the honest program is **4+2–3 nights** and **6–12 desk weeks**; if spec-on is slower, close the paper immediately and report “does it ever repay?” as answered negatively at the feasibility level.

docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/SYNTHESIS-PRAGMATICS-FIRST.md-13253-### 1. `mvp-icpe-upgrade` — fund, but as the corrected metrology capstone
docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/SYNTHESIS-PRAGMATICS-FIRST.md-13254-
docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/SYNTHESIS-PRAGMATICS-FIRST.md:13255:The submitted “ICPE upgrade” was correctly judged WEAK because its cross-window Q4 prediction is unauthorized and its WT310E arm is neither necessary nor securely available. The surviving paper is nevertheless the highest-certainty and highest-priority portfolio item: the calibrated instrument, attribution limit, floor calculus, refusal protocol, D-117 floors, and prospective decode contrast. Add Window C’s held-out floor-validation ladder, not the proposed multi-night workload matrix. Honest cost is **four planned nights, about 11.2–13.2 quiet hours, 3–6 desk weeks, plus one reserved rerun slot**. Estimated first-pass survival of all four windows is only **60–70%** given the project’s history; completion with one governed reserve is roughly **80–90%**. This is the only item that must proceed regardless of every later ranking.

docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/SYNTHESIS-PRAGMATICS-FIRST.md-13257-### 2. `quantization-ladder` — the best second-paper bet
docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/SYNTHESIS-PRAGMATICS-FIRST.md-13258-
docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/SYNTHESIS-PRAGMATICS-FIRST.md:13259:The VIABLE verdict holds only after shrinking to **BF16/Q4/Q8**, deleting Q5/Q6, deleting the unbuilt JouleWise quality gate, and framing the result as precision- and kernel-specific *resolvability*, not quality-neutral efficiency. The D-117 1.5B Q4 floor and exact 128/512 workload carry directly into the paper. BF16 and Q8 still need their own floors, followed by a three-arm contrast: **4+3 nights**, **4–8 incremental desk weeks**, and one reserve slot. A BF16–Q4 result should be loud; Q4–Q8 is the scientifically useful anomaly test and may resolve or refuse. Estimated survival after the capability smoke is **65–75%**. This is lower novelty than a mechanism paper, but far lower operational risk and the best match to the priority rule.
docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/SYNTHESIS-PRAGMATICS-FIRST.md-13260-
docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/SYNTHESIS-PRAGMATICS-FIRST.md-13261-### 3. `moe-routing-energy` — stretch, re-anchored and more expensive
docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/SYNTHESIS-PRAGMATICS-FIRST.md-13262-
docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/SYNTHESIS-PRAGMATICS-FIRST.md:13263:The VIABLE judgment is persuasive, but the 65 GB Qwen3.5-122B VLM/hybrid reasoning checkpoint should not be the claim vehicle. Use the referee’s re-anchor: **Qwen3-30B-A3B versus a dense Qwen3-4B partner**, with native-*k* versus forced-*k* as the causal within-checkpoint leg. This gives the paper both an interpretable dense comparison and a mechanism intervention. It also creates three separately scoped floor cells—native MoE, forced-*k* MoE, and dense—so the honest cost is **4+3–4 nights**, **6–12 desk weeks**, and a reserve, not two nights. Routing-sidecar overhead, output-divergence-induced routing locality, and projected floors can all kill it before collection. Estimated pre-night survival is **35–50%**. This is the right stretch because its ceiling is much higher than quantization’s, not because it is safer.

docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/SYNTHESIS-PRAGMATICS-FIRST.md:13267:The referee was right: this has the portfolio’s best framing—“from repeatability to resolvability”—and an unfundable portability experiment. The NVML/RAPL battery neither transports the phase-attribution finding nor respects existing fences. The surviving content is the MVP’s intellectual packaging plus Window C’s held-out effect ladder. Cost is therefore **the same four MVP nights**, with roughly **1–3 additional desk weeks** for the ladder analysis, refusal taxonomy, and prose. Probability of a useful result is **70–80%** because both correct refusals and correct resolutions support the thesis. Rank four reflects its value to the capstone, not authorization for a second manuscript.

docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/SYNTHESIS-PRAGMATICS-FIRST.md:13271:The proposal was WEAK because early-versus-late position is uncounterbalanceable and lacks a legitimate comparative floor. Its important discovery is different: attribution limitation is a **phase-boundary property**, not necessarily a global instrument property. Interior decode-chunk edges may be repeatability-limited near 0.3 J. First make that a desk-only MVP characterization figure. A later paper would need an intervention—bounded versus unbounded cache, or matched-position starting-KV variation—rather than observational token position. Claim-bearing cost is **4+1–2 nights** and **4–8 desk weeks** for chunk reduction, floor semantics, and refusal tests. Estimated survival after the runtime and floor gate is **45–60%**.

docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/SYNTHESIS-PRAGMATICS-FIRST.md-13274-
docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/SYNTHESIS-PRAGMATICS-FIRST.md:13275:The tag is WEAK as a three-paper portfolio, but its prefix-reuse idea is the only genuinely new asset-mined direction. The stated “crossover” is arithmetic—if building the cache is the avoided prefill, reuse wins at request two—while the empirical cache load/save overhead is probably below the instrument’s floor. The scientifically honest paper is therefore about what prefix reuse saves, what its SoC boundary misses in off-SoC cache I/O, and which overheads must be refused as unresolvable. Restrict to 2048/4096-token endpoints and mint matching gross/length floors inside **two extension windows**: **4+2 nights**, **3–5 desk weeks**, estimated survival **55–65%**. It is a credible alternate second paper if quantization dies at its desk gate.

docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/SYNTHESIS-PRAGMATICS-FIRST.md:13279:The original four-length, two-model “curve” is a borderline KILL: floor transport is anti-conservative, 7B faces the measured ~14 J comparative floor, and long-prefill thermal carryover is perfectly aligned with the claimed KV effect. A viable residue is one 1.5B long-context endpoint, longer decode to amplify the effect, a same-window long-context null floor, and a separate thermal-matched control. That is **two extension nights**, possibly three if the longer workload breaks the four-hour envelope: **4+2 planned, book 4+3**, with **3–6 desk weeks** and about **35–50%** survival. Do not arm 7B unless the fresh beta floor and local sizing independently support it.

   915	
   916	Options considered:
   917	
   918	1. No CI. Con: "tests pass" claims rest on local runs in handoff notes.
   919	2. Full matrix with extras (mlx cannot install on Linux runners; GPU absent).
   920	   Con: impossible or meaningless for hardware paths.
   921	3. Core-only CI: ubuntu runner, Python 3.11 and 3.14 (oldest supported per
   922	   `pyproject.toml`, plus the version observed in local development),
   923	   `python -m unittest discover -s tests` plus CLI smoke
   924	   (`validate-config` on both example configs). Later phases extend it with
   925	   the mock-bundle end-to-end run and `validate-bundle` once those exist.
   926	
   927	Decision: option 3.
   928	
   929	Considerations: the stdlib-only core (D-009) is exactly the testable surface
   930	on a hosted runner; hardware adapters are validated by run bundles, not CI.
 13290	- **`cross-runtime-contrast` — KILL.** It uses the wrong floor, confounds runtime with quantization bytes, lacks an adapter and quality gate, and really needs three new nights.
 13291	- **`drift-thermal-science` — KILL.** The standalone paper duplicates the MVP; keep only the desk-only “price of never-zero” subsection.
 13292	- **`energy-nutrition-label` — KILL.** The field schema is already the MVP; ship a validator and the negative 3080 Ti label as artifact material.
 13293	- **`mtp-energy` — KILL.** Native MTP is unsupported and a fork would become a runtime/instrument project; retain the dated negative AXI-SC result.
 13294	- **`open-explore-advisor` — KILL.** All three ideas are dominated; harvest only the §6 scope gap and the missing JouleSort/Mantis positioning.
 13295	- **`open-explore-contrarian` — KILL.** It proposes no actual course change; its sole contribution is the Window C versus descope ruling.
 13296	- **`open-explore-repo` — KILL.** Its Q4 and wall ideas duplicate other lanes; harvest the zero-night 20× time-anchor-defect figure.
 13297	- **`param-scaling-energy` — KILL.** The curve is foregone, the normalization is denominator-biased, and the instrument is irrelevant to the large effects.
 13298	- **`prefill-scaling-laws` — KILL.** Its floor transport is anti-conservative and honest cost is 7–8 extension nights; the 256-token arm remains a separate Ed option.
 13299	- **`refusal-as-result` — KILL.** Not a standalone paper; perform the census and PRE-WINDOW taxonomy/plumbing repair for the MVP.
 13300	- **`split-inference-metrology` — KILL.** The split winner is unmeasurable across the declared boundaries; fund only the one-evening GPU-cadence probe.
 13301	- **`tokenizer-honesty` — KILL as written.** The desk study reproduces 2023 work; a real non-Latin ranking-flip experiment would cost **two to three**, not one, nights once both stack floors and the contrast are counted.
 13302	- **`wall-meter-validation` — KILL as a paper.** C8 can be an MVP/ICPE boundary-transfer section if loan, battery, fan, fixture, and synchronization gates pass; one meter cannot validate `powermetrics` gain or phase attribution.
 13303	
 13304	## Recommended paper arc
 13305	
 13306	### Fall 2026 — MVP capstone: “From Repeatability to Resolvability”
 13307	
 13308	Before any night:
 13309	
 13310	1. Finish D-117 U1–U8: bracket sessions, successor construction, multi-cell minting, campaign packs, extraction specifications, three-window regression, and readiness validation.
 13311	2. Land the urgent refusal plumbing: `member_id → reason_code` in verdict rows and all 16 shadow window-verdict codes under the ratified refusal specification.
 13312	3. Decide Window C scope and the 256-token arm.
 13313	4. Keep every salvage reducer read-only and outside the D-117 refusal path.
 13314	
 13315	Then collect, in D-117 order:
 13316	
 13317	| Window | Purpose | Planned occupancy |
 13318	|---|---|---:|
 13319	| Alpha | 1.5B decode floor + prefill rider | 3.14 h |
 13320	| Beta | 7B decode floor + prefill rider | 3.24 h |
 13321	| Gamma | 1.5B-versus-7B decode contrast | 2.80 h |
 13322	| Window C | §6 characterization and held-out floor-validation ladder | 2–4 h |
 13323	| Reserved, not planned | One governed rerun/contingency | 2–4 h |
 13324	
 13325	Alpha and beta must pass and mint before gamma’s armwise floor gate is finalized. Window C follows all three, as D-117 clause 4 requires. November–December should be paper, artifact, claims-audit, and advisor time—not another experiment wave.
 13326	
 13327	### Spring 2027 — second paper: shrunk quantization ladder
 13328	
 13329	After the capstone data and claims are locked:
 13330	
 13331	1. Run the BF16/Q8 capability and sizing gates.
 13332	2. Collect the BF16 floor.
 13333	3. Collect the Q8 floor.
 13334	4. Collect the BF16/Q4/Q8 contrast.
 13335	5. Reserve one rerun slot but do not pre-authorize outcome-driven top-ups.
 13336	6. Hold at least six weeks after data freeze for the claims audit, artifact dry-run, advisor review, and venue compression.
 13337	
 13338	### Late Spring/Summer 2027 — stretch: re-anchored MoE
 13339	
 13340	Run only the desk feasibility program during the semester. Collect MoE nights only if routing evidence is bufferable, overhead is bounded, outputs and routing locality remain interpretable, and the three floor cells fit a frozen 3–4-night plan. Otherwise stop with quantization as the second paper and MoE as well-evidenced future work.
 13341	
 13342	## Night budget
 13343	
 13344	| Milestone | Planned claim/characterization nights | Reserved slots | Cumulative planned |
 13345	|---|---:|---:|---:|
 13346	| Complete MVP | 4 | 1 | 4 |
 13347	| Through quantization paper | +3 | +1 | 7 |
 13348	| Through MoE stretch | +3–4 | +1 | 10–11 |
 13349	| Optional 256-token prefill contrast | +1 | potentially +1 | add only by Ed ruling |
 13350	
 13351	Thus the firm commitment should be **seven planned nights through the second paper**, with two calendar reserves. Do not precommit the MoE nights.
 13352	
 13353	## Salvage placement
 13354	
 13355	| Salvage | Correct home | Marginal night cost |
 13356	|---|---|---:|
 13357	| Held-out floor-validation ladder | MVP Window C / §6 | Included in night 4 |
 13358	| “Price of never-zero” arithmetic | MVP §4 subsection | 0 |
 13359	| 20× time-anchor-defect cautionary figure | MVP motivation/characterization | 0 |
 13360	| Contamination over 203 idle captures | MVP §5/§6 admission-gate evaluation | 0 |
 13361	| Refusal census and reconstructability denominator | MVP C-iii + artifact | 0 |
 13362	| `member_id → reason_code` and 16-code scope repair | PRE-WINDOW operational requirement | 0 |
 13363	| Interior-chunk noise-limited estimand | MVP characterization appendix first | 0 initially |
 13364	| Negative 3080 Ti label | MVP reporting/artifact demonstration | 0 |
 13365	| KV-context ABBA | Alternate second paper if quantization dies | 1–2, realistically 2 |
 13366	| Prefix-reuse boundary/refusal | Alternate KV paper | 2 |
 13367	| Non-Latin tokenizer ranking flip | Later reporting paper only | 2–3 |
 13368	| Spec-decode tok/s pilot | Gate on a future mechanism paper | 2 daytime hours |
 13369	| A4 static-batch adapter | Infrastructure, not a paper | 0 |
 13370	| GPU-cadence probe | Split future-work evidence | 1 evening |
 13371	
 13372	## Synergy map
 13373	
 13374	- **Alpha’s Q4 floor is the central quantization saving.** Exact model, workload, runtime, phase and stack identity let Q4 serve as the middle quantization rung, eliminating one floor night.
 13375	- **D-117’s pinset-v2 and multi-cell mint machinery lowers desk cost** for quantization and MoE, but it does not transport any numerical floor to a different stack.
 13376	- **Window C can serve four MVP needs at once:** empirical floor behavior, magnitude/null response, linearity, and between-session evidence. It can inform later length-sweep transport rules, but does not automatically authorize them.
 13377	- **The 203 idle captures are already collected as part of D-117.** The contamination analysis is therefore a zero-night evaluation of the admission gate.
 13378	- **Refusal plumbing benefits every downstream paper.** Fixing it before Alpha gives the MVP, quantization, and MoE machine-attributable negative evidence.
 13379	- **Quantization shares model, tokenizer, workload, adapter, manifest grammar and reporting with Alpha.** MoE shares only the generic machinery; its floors and attribution basis remain independent.
 13380	- **The MoE dense and routed arms share runtime and tokenizer**, allowing one multi-arm science window, but each still needs a separate floor cell.
 13381	- **A4 batch work and the spec-decode pilot are desk synergies, not reasons to fund batch nights.**
 13382	- **GPU cadence benefits split feasibility only.** It cannot validate the Mac floor or a cross-device composite clock bound.
 13383	
 13384	## Single best second-paper bet: BF16/Q4/Q8 quantization
 13385	
 13386	Why it wins:
 13387	
 13388	- It has the most direct claim-grade reuse: Alpha supplies Q4’s floor.
 13389	- It needs no new hardware, runtime fork, cross-device clock, serving policy, or unowned meter.
 13390	- One contrast is almost guaranteed to resolve, while Q4–Q8 remains a real question.
 13391	- A refusal is scientifically coherent: “these rungs cannot be ranked at this workload under the calibrated instrument.”
 13392	- Its operational failures are mostly desk-visible before a night.
 13393	
 13394	Honest cost is **three incremental claim nights, 4–8 desk weeks, and one reserve**. From today, reaching this second paper means **seven planned nights and roughly 7–14 cumulative desk weeks including the MVP critical path**.
 13395	
 13396	### Kill-gate schedule
 13397	
 13398	1. **Before any secondary D-016/artifact commitment:** two-hour pinned-version smoke. Establish one BF16 source revision; reproducibly derive Q4 and Q8; load all three; verify tokenizer, module allowlist, memory, requested output policy, and conversion receipts. Any unexplained structural difference kills the paper.
 13399	
 13400	2. **Within one week after Alpha mints the fresh Q4 floor:** run off-window diagnostic timing/energy probes on the exact 128/512 workload. Project Q4–Q8 against the fresh Q4 floor and a conservative Q8 floor range. Kill if Q4–Q8 is clearly below the projected armwise decision bar and Ed does not want a paper whose only resolved result is the trivial BF16–Q4 contrast.
 13401	
 13402	3. **Before freezing either floor window:** prove each 50-member plan fits below four hours with 20% margin. BF16 is the risk because its larger weight traffic may invalidate the Q4-based runtime envelope. If it does not fit without changing workload identity, kill or redesign before a night.
 13403	
 13404	4. **Before night one:** freeze the three-cell mint/consumer schema, multi-arm estimator, Holm family, output-divergence reporting, and the D-041 posture: no JouleWise-issued quality-equivalence claim. Published quality evidence may contextualize the exact rungs; it may not be converted into an internal accuracy paper.
 13405	
 13406	5. **After each floor:** a failed whole-window verdict or a floor much larger than projected stops the contrast unless the previously frozen cause-removal retry applies. No top-ups.
 13407	
 13408	6. **After the contrast:** report the frozen outcome, including refusal. Do not add Q5/Q6 after seeing Q4–Q8.
 13409	
 13410	## Open questions for Ed, ranked
 13411	
 13412	1. **Does the MVP retain C-iv?** Recommend: fund Window C as night 4. If not, rewrite the abstract, contribution list and §6 now to declare full characterization future work; do not submit an empty promised contribution.
 13413	
 13414	2. **Does the 256-token prefill contrast become night 5?** Recommend: no for the capstone. Keep gamma decode-only and publish the 128-token marginality as prospective sizing evidence. If adopted, it needs its own plan, evidence root and matching prefill floors; it cannot be attached casually to gamma.
 13415	
 13416	3. **May Alpha/Beta pre-register reported phase-energy cells in addition to their floor cells?** Recommend: yes only if the ruling confirms no added members, runtime or floor semantics. This is time-critical before the campaign-pack hashes freeze and improves reuse for quantization and future ladders.
 13417	
 13418	4. **What are the actual capstone, advisor-review and venue evidence-by dates?** Without them, “Fall” and “Spring” cannot be converted into safe last-arm dates. Reserve six post-data weeks and one MVP rerun slot first.
 13419	
 13420	5. **Authorize the shrunk quantization posture?** The decision is BF16/Q4/Q8, no Q5/Q6, no internal 256-item quality verdict, and three extension nights. Recommend yes, conditional on the smoke.
 13421	
 13422	6. **What evidence may enter the public artifact?** Decide whether sanitized bundles, refusal rows, calibration receipts and raw idle traces may be archived. This affects the strongest zero-night contribution.
 13423	
 13424	7. **Which mechanism owns the stretch slot?** Recommend re-anchored MoE after quantization. Spec decode receives only its two-hour pilot; MTP remains closed; split receives only the cadence probe.
 13425

The provenance check is decisive: Alpha’s pinned Q4 says it was converted with `mlx-lm 0.18.1`, while the proposed ladder pin is `mlx-lm 0.31.3`; its card does not record the upstream source revision. The executable plan therefore has to treat byte-identical Q4 reproduction as Gate 1’s first hard test. Without it, the adopted “three nights / Alpha reused” budget is not valid.

Log</h1> <p>This is the canonical record of design decisions for JouleWise. Every decision that binds later work, trades off real alternatives, or would otherwise need to be re-derived by a future agent gets an entry here.</p> <h2 id="how-to-use-this-log">How To Use This Log</h2> <ul> <li>Before implementing anything non-trivial, check whether a decision here already covers it. Do not silently re-decide settled questions.</li> <li>When you make a new decision of this kind during a run, add an entry, link it from the run report, and reference its ID (<code>D-NNN</code>) in the code review or doc that applies it.</li> <li>Statuses: <code>accepted</code> (binding until revisited), <code>open</code> (criteria defined, evidence pending), <code>proposed</code> (recorded, awaiting Ed&#39;s ratification), <code>superseded by D-NNN</code>.</li> <li>Every entry must include Options Considered and Considerations. A decision without recorded alternatives is not auditable.</li> <li>Revisit triggers are part of the contract: when a trigger fires, the decision must be re-examined, not quietly worked around.</li> </ul> <h2 id="index">Index</h2> <div class="table-scroll"><table> <thead> <tr> <th>ID</th> <th>Title</th> <th>Status</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody><tr> <td>D-001</td> <td>Run bundles store normalized <code>config.json</code>, not YAML</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-002</td> <td>Telemetry sampling via subprocess + file, no controller threading</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-003</td> <td>Timestamp and clock-alignment policy</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-004</td> <td><code>powermetrics</code> privilege workflow</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-005</td> <td>One bundle per repetition, grouped by experiment manifest</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-006</td> <td>Dashboard v1 is a static HTML report generator</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-007</td> <td>YAML config input is deferred</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-008</td> <td>Split runs arrive via schema v0.2 (<code>run_kind</code> + <code>split_plan</code>)</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-009</td> <td>Dependency policy: stdlib core, optional extras</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-010</td> <td>Run ID scheme</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-011</td> <td><code>summary_metrics.json</code> is the bundle completion marker</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-012</td> <td>Failure-reason to run-status mapping</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-013</td> <td>Controller-as-DUT mitigation for Mac-local runs</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-014</td> <td>Statistical protocol for repeated runs</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-015</td> <td>Split-mechanism priority and same-runtime rule</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-016</td> <td>Benchmark model selection</td> <td>open (provisional small-model pick 2026-07-06;
